text:
There's a line in Paul's first letter to the Thessalonians that Peter Thiel keeps coming back to: "For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them." In his lectures on the Antichrist, which he's now given in San Francisco, Rome and Nashville, he treats "peace and safety" as the slogan the Antichrist will run on. I've been thinking about that for a long time, because if you take the theology out, what's left is a serious claim about technology and power: in a frightened world, the most dangerous person is the one who promises to keep it safe.

The reasoning goes like this. Every few decades there's a new way the world might end. After 1945 it was nuclear war, later it was climate change and pandemics, and now it's AI. Each one comes with the same offer: give someone enough authority and the disaster can be prevented. Thiel calls this the choice between "Antichrist or Armageddon," and his point is that we treat the first option as if it costs nothing.

It's worth asking what that authority would actually need. A technology that's banned in every country but one hasn't been banned. To really stop something, you'd need a power that reaches every country, knows about every weapons program and can see what every large computer is running. However good its intentions, that's a world government with nothing outside its reach, and I don't see how it avoids becoming totalitarian.

What makes this hard to dismiss is that Thiel doesn't have to imagine that government. Some of the people most worried about AI have already described it. In 2019 the philosopher Nick Bostrom wrote a paper called "The Vulnerable World Hypothesis," arguing that if some future technology turned out to be cheap and destructive enough, surviving it might require near-total surveillance, a "high-tech panopticon," along with effective global governance. He wasn't hoping for it. He was saying it might be the price. Eliezer Yudkowsky went further in a 2023 piece in Time, calling for a worldwide halt to training large AI models, tracking of the chips they run on, and a willingness to bomb datacenters that refused to comply.

Thiel has called Yudkowsky, Bostrom and Greta Thunberg "legionnaires of the Antichrist." I think that's unfair to them. They're afraid of real things, and some of those things deserve fear. But the question he's pointing at is fair, and the people asking for a global pause rarely answer it: who holds the off switch, and what stops them from using it for everything else?

Yudkowsky matters to Thiel for another reason too. In the late '90s, he was one of the most optimistic people anywhere about superintelligence, which he hoped would cure aging and eventually death. In 2000 he co-founded the institute that's now called MIRI, and Thiel was one of its biggest early donors. His latest book is titled If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies, and Thiel says he's embarrassed he ever funded him. For Thiel, that turn, from expecting technology to defeat death to expecting it to kill everyone, is what happened to the whole culture, and it's the fear that makes "peace and safety" sound reasonable.

It also explains why Thiel sees no conflict between his faith and his interest in longevity, which he's funded for years. The usual objection is that wanting to live forever is a kind of rebellion against God, but in his reading the Bible is on the other side. Christianity doesn't promise a soul drifting off to heaven. That's closer to Plato. It promises a body raised from the dead, in a world where nobody dies. Paul calls death "the last enemy." In Matthew 10, among the instructions Jesus gives the twelve is "raise the dead," and in Acts both Peter and Paul do it. On this point I think he's right. Whatever you make of the longevity project, it isn't obviously un-Christian.

Seen that way, science had a destination, and Thiel thinks it has lost sight of it. Francis Bacon, who did more than anyone to found the experimental method, wrote a whole book on prolonging human life. Today a growing number of countries, Canada among them, let doctors help patients die. That's a harder subject than Thiel allows it to be, and it shouldn't be reduced to a talking point, but the change in direction is real.

Underneath all of this is a bigger claim: that science is a Christian inheritance in the first place. Part of the argument is about time. Much of the ancient world thought history repeats itself. The Stoics believed the universe burns up and is rebuilt, the same every time, and if that's how things work, there's little reason to try to improve anything. Scripture tells a story with a start and an end, and the end is better. Daniel 12:4 says "many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased," and Bacon printed that verse on the title page of his 1620 book on the new method. Thiel calls Daniel "the first true historian."

The other part comes from René Girard, Thiel's teacher at Stanford. Girard thought people copy each other's desires, become rivals because of it, and restore peace by uniting against a scapegoat whose guilt everyone takes for granted. In his reading, the Gospels are the first story told from the scapegoat's side, insisting the victim was innocent, and that makes the old mechanism harder to run. Thiel's example is the witch trials. Two of their most important early critics were believers. The physician Johann Weyer wrote in 1563 that the accused women were mostly sick and confused. The Jesuit Friedrich Spee argued in 1631 that torture would get a confession out of anyone, and that many of the condemned were innocent. If no witch spoiled the harvest, then something else did, and finding out what is the work of science.

This is the strongest historical part of his case, though it isn't as clean as he presents it. The trials were run by Christians of both churches, and Weyer and Spee were arguing against their own. Greek and Islamic scholars did serious science long before Europe's Scientific Revolution. Christianity produced both the persecution and the arguments that ended it, which Girard would probably say is the whole point.

As for who the Antichrist might be, Thiel won't name anyone. In Nashville he said "I don't think I'm the Antichrist," and he doesn't expect a tech billionaire either. His guess is a charismatic politician aiming for the American presidency. He also kept returning to the age of 33, when Alexander the Great died after conquering most of the known world, and roughly when Jesus died, to show how much a single life can change in a short time. Alexander needed armies. Someone who inherits a surveillance system built for our safety wouldn't.

Is anything holding that back? In his second letter to the Thessalonians, Paul says the "man of lawlessness" can't come until whatever restrains him is "taken out of the way." The Greek word is katechon, and Paul never says what it is. Early writers like Tertullian thought it was Rome, and in the 20th century the German legal theorist Carl Schmitt revived the idea. Thiel's candidate, in a lecture titled "New Rome," is the United States, the only country with the ideology, the military and the financial reach of an empire. "When the US is done," he said, "the West is done, and the world is done."

The twist that follows is the most interesting part of the whole series. Anything strong enough to restrain the Antichrist is strong enough to become him, and if a one-world state ever comes, the likeliest source is the one country that already reaches everywhere. Thiel called America "ground zero of the one-world state" and "ground zero of the resistance to the one-world state." The protector and the threat could be the same system, with a different person in charge.

There are real problems with all of this. The biggest is that the theory can't lose. Any new AI regulation can be read as a step toward the world state, and any warning about risk as the Antichrist's slogan, so nothing that happens could show him he's wrong. The Nashville Scene's reviewer complained that across about six hours, he gave very few specifics. And it matters who's talking. Thiel co-founded Palantir, which sells data software to governments, militaries and intelligence agencies, and he has a lot of money riding on AI. That doesn't make the warning wrong, but it's a reason to read it carefully.

Thiel likes to ask founders what important truth very few people agree with them on. His own answer seems to be that the catastrophe isn't the only thing to fear, and that whoever offers to save us from it may be worse. I'm not sure it needs the Antichrist to be true. AI can be dangerous, and the people saying so aren't crazy. But it's much easier to picture the world ending in a dramatic disaster than ending quietly, with everyone agreeing it was for their own safety, and the second picture is the one Thiel wants people to see.

text:
When you're trying to break a habit, the craving is only part of the problem. The other part is the thinking that won't stop around it.

You go over the last relapse again and again, and you argue with yourself about whether one more time would really matter.

Psychologists call this rumination, which means going over the same thoughts again and again without getting anywhere. For a lot of people, the habit was the fastest way to switch that noise off, and that's what turns rumination into a trigger.

A study from Stanford looked at what turns it down.

In 2015, a team led by Gregory Bratman sent 38 people who lived in cities on a 90-minute walk. Half of them walked through quiet parkland with grass and trees, and the other half walked along a busy road. The people who walked in nature said they were going over the same thoughts less afterwards. Brain scans showed less activity in an area at the front of the brain called the subgenual prefrontal cortex, which tends to be more active when people are stuck on sad or worrying thoughts. The people who walked by the road didn't show either change.

Both groups walked for the same time and got the same exercise, so the difference came from where they walked.

Now think about where your rumination usually happens. You're on the couch or in bed with your phone in your hand, indoors and sitting still, going over the same thoughts. The longer it goes on, the louder the craving gets, and the habit offers you a quick way out of your own head.

A walk outside is another way out, and it doesn't cost you anything.

This was a small study, with healthy people who weren't trying to stop anything, so it doesn't prove that a walk will stop a craving. What it does show is that where you spend your time can change how much your mind keeps circling the same thing.

So what do we do about it in my program?

In phase 1, before clients have even stopped the habit, one of the daily non-negotiables is what we call an introspection walk. It's 8,000 to 10,000 steps a day, with at least half of it while the sun is out, because daylight also helps set your body clock for sleep.

The walk is time to think. You take whatever is going around in your head and work through it while you move, instead of sitting with it on the couch. It also gets you out of the house during the hours when boredom would usually set in, and boredom is one of the biggest triggers there is.

We put it in early on purpose. By the time clients stop the habit, the walk is already part of their day, so when the thinking starts, they already have somewhere to take it.

None of this makes cravings go away by itself. But it gives your mind a way to settle down that isn't the habit.

This is how you get out of your own head without the habit.

週明けの米株式市場は、AnthropicのS-1正式提出を好感してSOX指数が2.8%急反発したほか、メガテックの資本政策と企業再編を巡る大ニュースが相次ぎました。WSJ・MarketWatchの報道から、今後の投資判断に直結する3つの地殻変動を紹介します。

1. Anthropicの公式S-1提出が照らす「AI経済圏の光と影」

先週の観測報道を経てAnthropicが正式に上場申請を行いました。
急激な売上拡大が確認されたことで市場のAIセンチメントは一旦持ち直しましたが、本質的な論点は「未曾有の計算コスト負担」と「長期利益信託（Long-Term Benefit Trust）による株主統治の制約」にあります。上場を通じて巨額の外部資金を公募市場から調達する道筋がついたものの、投資家がこのビジネスモデルにどれほどのマルチプルを許容するかが、今後のハイテクバリュエーションの新たな基準値となります。

2. Metaの「950億ドル調達」と半導体ベンダー出資の共生関係

Metaが発表した最大950億ドルの資金調達計画において、NvidiaやAMD、Broadcomが株式を引き受ける可能性が浮上した点は極めて象徴的です。
「GPUを売る半導体巨頭が、最大の顧客であるハイパースケーラーの増資を引き受け、その資金で再びGPUを買わせる」というベンダーファイナンス的な資本の循環構造が形成されつつあります。AIインフラの拡張がメガテック単独のバランスシートを超え、サプライチェーン全体の相互依存・共同戦線へと移行している証左です。

If I have to choose one of them it is clearly $AMZN by a wide margin because only $AMZN have a business which is the Everything Store which has a massive moat of the warehouse and shipment network, brand loyalty, and millions of customers who use the established business to buy a broad range of physical items in multiple countries. Their business won't go away if the world is flooded with free open weight models or if new technology developments make LLMs need 100 times less compute, or if AI replaces all apps. Note that if high inflation drives up prices of goods generally, then Amazon's cut of sales revenues goes up with in line with the inflated prices. Counter argument is that a deep recession would cause people to cut back on purchases to only buy necessities (which affects almost every company).

Second choice would be Microsoft because they are so deeply embedded in every medium to large corporation on the planet, every law firm, every accounting firm. Also my impression (which might be out of date) is that Microsoft have been quite savvy to get AI technology from their OpenAI relationship without over the top massive expenditure that OpenAI has exposed itself to. If open weight models kill OpenAI and Anthropic then Microsoft will still do well, because they can offer AI integration to their existing corporate clients (Microsoft systems are full of corporate data, so Microsoft are well positioned to offer AI services that use that corporate data, and Microsoft don't care where the models come from so long as they work).

If I don't have to choose one of them, I probably want to shelter my cash during the coming AI bubble collapse far from tech in oil, other energy, consumer staples (Nestle and similar), and companies that have tollbooth businesses with moats where their income will track the coming massive inflation (e.g. VISA, Mastercard).

I want to own companies that:
(A) Sell something that everyone needs to use, or will never give up using, like their smartphone or their electronic payments network, or food, or shelter, or energy for transport and home heating / cooling, or healthcare, or in the USA their car. Note that smartphone is not optional as it is required for biometric identity verification to access banking, but people can keep their Smartphone much longer on average before replacement.
(B) Sell something that can't be printed or created by AI or government (so I don't want publishing, films, music, or fiat currency)
(C) Have an internationally diverse business income
(D) Have a moat
(E) Will do well in the face of massive inflation, so needs to have pricing power or naturally follows inflation because they take a cut of a flow of money.
(F) Will survive a deep recession.

An obvous sector that will suffer badly is airlines as they are so dependent on the price of jet fuel, and energy prices are going to go up due to destruction of refineries and other energy infrastructure in Russia and in Middle Eastern nations. I predict that air travel will return to the 1970s model where only a "jet set" of wealthy people can afford to fly.

This is crazy. Absolutely insane.

We were told the AI boom would create a massive wave of new tech jobs. Instead, Microsoft just offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees, nearly 27% of its entire workforce.

I know this isn't a mandatory layoff, but it's a clear sign of how much cash the AI infrastructure race is burning. Building data centers for OpenAI, Anthropic and cloud customers is so expensive that Microsoft is actively trying to shrink its payroll to protect cash flow.

Ironically, even the teams building Copilot and AI Experiences are on the buyout list.

- Scope: Around 60,000 employees out of 223,000 globally are eligible across the US, India, UK, and Canada.
- Seniority: Open to Level 70 and below.
- Who's included: AI Experiences, Copilot, Xbox, Windows + Devices, Finance, and HR. Sales, Marketing, and Security are excluded.
- The package: Standard severance, with a minimum of 60 days of base pay on payroll, scaling up to 39 weeks of base pay depending on level and tenure.
- Timeline: Employees must decide by early December, with their last day set for December 31.

text:
Kalshi just became the NBA's official prediction market partner.

We went through the court records, regulator filings and Kalshi's own statements. 

Here's what this announcement left out:

1/
The deal makes Kalshi a "Preferred Prediction Market Exchange of the NBA."
Kalshi gets NBA logos, marketing rights and official league data to settle its NBA markets. Polymarket got the same deal.
2/
Here's what makes it strange.
In May 2025, after Kalshi started offering spreads and moneylines on NBA games, an NBA lawyer wrote to federal regulators asking for protections against the integrity risks of prediction markets.
17 months later, Kalshi is a partner.
3/
The NBA has reason to worry.
Former Raptor Jontay Porter admitted he left games early to help bettors who bet the "under" on his stats. He pleaded guilty to federal wire fraud conspiracy and was banned for life.
4/
In October 2025, the FBI arrested Terry Rozier in a case centered on a March 2023 game he left after less than 10 minutes. Sportsbooks had flagged suspicious betting on his stats.
The NBA reviewed that game in 2023 and found no rule violation.
Rozier has pleaded not guilty. His trial is set for February 2027.
5/
To be clear, those bets ran through sportsbooks, not Kalshi.
But they show where the risk is: inside information about who plays and who's hurt.
6/
Kalshi listed markets on exactly that.
It offered contracts on athlete injuries, including how long players would be sidelined and whether specific NFL players would suit up for Week 1.
Kalshi has since pulled them.
7/
Then there's Giannis Antetokounmpo.
He became a Kalshi shareholder in a deal signed on NBA trade deadline day. Earlier that week, Kalshi listed markets on where he'd be traded.
Kalshi says the deal wasn't in place while those markets ran, his stake is under 1%, and he's barred from trading NBA markets.
8/
Kalshi says it isn't a sportsbook.
But its ads promoted sports betting as legal in all 50 states. And according to a federal appeals court, sports made up 95% of its 2025 revenue.
In August, that court ruled 3-0 that Kalshi's sports contracts are, in substance, sports gambling.
9/
In most states you must be 21 to bet on the NBA at a sportsbook. On Kalshi, it's 18.
CNN estimates 18-to-21-year-olds traded $5.4 billion on Kalshi so far this year. Kalshi has also recruited "ambassadors" on college campuses.
10/
Sportsbooks let problem gamblers ban themselves through state self-exclusion programs.
A Massachusetts man who had self-excluded says in a lawsuit that Kalshi offered no such option, and that he lost tens of thousands of dollars there in one month.
11/
Kalshi's ads said "We aren't the house."
But Kalshi owns a trading company, Kalshi Trading, that takes the other side of some customer bets.
And Bloomberg reported that Jump Trading agreed to take an equity stake in Kalshi in exchange for trading on the platform.
12/
So who wins?
Kalshi's own data: over 70% of traders lost money over six months.
Over the long run, traders and analysts surveyed by How Gambling Works estimate only 2–5% of users come out ahead.
13/
Then there's the fine print.
Traders put more than $54 million on whether Iran's Supreme Leader would be "out." When he died, Kalshi paid at the last price before his death, about 40¢ instead of $1, citing a rule about death.
It refunded fees and net losses. Traders sued anyway.
14/
In January, Kalshi didn't pay winners on some NFL season markets.
It paid them after users complained publicly.

@Matthew24906171 @KalishJr @James_Hawke1 @NardMyWally 
one of the best flat earth photos I’ve ever taken. From Criterion Summit Mountain identifier. 

Criterion Summit (Wasco County, Oregon) is the mountain pass and roadside viewpoint on U.S. Route 197 south of Maupin (about 7 miles north of the US 197/US 97 junction). Elevation is roughly 3,360 ft (1,020–1,025 m). It is near the historic unincorporated community of Criterion. 
A sign and viewpoint map (sometimes called a “mountain finder”) mark the summit and identify Cascade Range peaks visible on clear days, ranging from Broken Top to the southwest through peaks such as the Sisters and Mount Jefferson to Mount Adams to the northwest. Local sources also note views of Mount Hood. 
Approximate straight-line distances to major Cascade peaks
These are calculated from the summit’s coordinates (~44.98°N, 120.99°W):
•  Mount Hood (~11,249 ft): ~44 miles
•  Mount Jefferson (~10,500 ft): ~45 miles
•  Broken Top / South Sister area (~9,000–10,360 ft): ~71–72 miles
•  Mount Adams (~12,276 ft): ~88 miles
Visibility depends on clear weather; the open high-desert setting helps with long-distance views.
Nearby local summits/peaks (examples)
From peak databases and topo sources around Criterion Summit:
•  Shaniko Butte: ~17.7 miles
•  Nachter Butte: ~17.8 miles
•  Sugarloaf: ~17.9 miles
•  Cross Hill: ~18.2 miles
•  Friends Peak: ~20 miles
•  Mutton Mountain: ~21 miles
The area also includes the nearby BLM Criterion Tract, which offers open views of the Cascades, the Deschutes River canyon, and local features such as the Mutton Mountains.

FBI releases video of shooter who killed Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University
RESTRICTION: USERS MUST CREDIT “FBI” HANDOUT —EDITORIAL USE ONLY —

SHOTLIST:

UTAH, UNITED STATES (SEPT. 10, 2025) (FBI - RESTRICTED)

1. VARIOUS CCTV FOOTAGE OF SUSPECT JUMPING FROM ROOFTOP OF BUILDING, FLEEING FROM SCENE UTAH, UNITED STATES - SEPT. 10, 2025 - RESTRICTION: USERS MUST CREDIT “FBI” HANDOUT —EDITORIAL USE ONLY — The FBI on Thursday, Sept. 11, released video footage of the shooter involved in the fatal attack at Utah Valley University that left American conservative commentator Charlie Kirk dead.

Authorities said the footage shows the suspect jumping from the rooftop of a building shortly after the September 10 shooting before fleeing the scene. Investigators recovered a firearm and ammunition abandoned in a wooded area near the university.

Trace evidence collected from the rooftop included shoe impressions, a forearm imprint, and a palm print, according to officials.

The FBI released additional photos Thursday of a person of interest tied to the shooting of American conservative commentator Charlie Kirk.

“The FBI continues to work alongside our law enforcement partners to seek justice in the murder of Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025. We are releasing additional photos of a person of interest,” the bureau wrote on the US social media company X’s platform.

The four grainy photos appear to depict a college-age male clad in a black long-sleeve t-shirt, jeans, a backpack, a baseball cap and black sunglasses.

This comes as the FBI offered a reward of up to $100,000 for information leading to the arrest of the person who fatally shot Kirk.

"The FBI is offering a reward of up to $100,000 for information leading to the identification and arrest of the individual(s) responsible for the murder of Charlie Kirk on September 10, 2025, at Utah Valley University in Orem, Utah," the bureau wrote on X.

Earlier Thursday, the bureau released a pair of photos of a "person of interest" in the fatal shooting of the American right-wing commentator, appealing to the public for assistance in identifying the individual.

Kirk, 31, was fatally shot Wednesday while addressing a group of students at Utah Valley University in the city of Orem, some 40 miles (64.4 kilometers) south of Salt Lake City. The apparent targeted attack occurred despite security, including six university police officers and Kirk's private team.

Online videos captured the moment a bullet struck Kirk as he spoke, sending students fleeing in panic. He was rushed to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead hours later.

The FBI said investigators found a "high-powered bolt-action rifle" that was recovered in a wooded area linked to the suspected shooter's escape route.

Multiple media reports suggested that ammunition engraved with "transgender and antifascist ideology" was found in the rifle. The reports cited an internal law enforcement document.

The New York Times cited an anonymous senior law enforcement official who stressed that the information had not been verified, did not match other summaries of evidence and may have been misread.

The investigation has so far been able to track the suspect's movements starting roughly 30 minutes before Kirk was shot, Utah Department of Public Safety Commissioner Beau Mason said during a news conference. Authorities believe the suspect arrived near the Utah Valley University campus at 11.52 am local time (1752GMT) and made his way to the roof and to what Robert Bohls, the FBI special agent in charge of the Salt Lake City field office, described as a "shooting location."

After the shooting, the suspect moved to the other side of the building, jumped down and made his way into a nearby neighborhood where investigators have sought home camera surveillance footage.

Two people of interest were taken into custody in the aftermath of the shooting but were later released after being cleared of suspicion. Mason said both faced "threats" after being released and asked the public to be "patient with the investigative process."

"These individuals were not suspects. They were people of interest. We ask that you do not impose into those people and that investigative process. They don't deserve that harassment," said Mason.

text:
That’s a fair criticism, and mathematically, you’re largely correct. My proposal deliberately preserves the Electoral College’s existing state weighting, including the advantage smaller states receive.

I don’t believe any American inherently deserves a more powerful vote because of where they live. That’s a legitimate weakness of the current system that my proposal doesn’t fully eliminate.

What I’m trying to accomplish is proportional representation within each state. A Republican in California or a Democrat in Wyoming would contribute toward their candidate’s national electoral total, even when their preferred candidate loses the state.

I recognize that a national popular vote offers greater equality between individual voters. My concern is preserving some balance between population-based representation and the federal structure, while reducing winner-take-all distortions and the disproportionate attention given to competitive states.

It’s a compromise, and I think it’s worth debating whether that compromise is preferable to either alternative.

Old Flame (Gambler's Folly Book 4) by Mellie Miller is a heartfelt second-chance paranormal shifter romance that blends emotional healing, mature love, and the magic of fate. Billionaire and bear shifter Kort Behrens has been lucky in business but unlucky in love—after two failed marriages and a string of gold diggers, he’s given up hope of finding a real connection. Elizabeth Murphy, a widow for four years, has rebuilt her life through her Reiki practice and the quiet companionship of her cat, Puzzle, still carrying the quiet ache of a long marriage that never fully satisfied her deeper desires. When these old college friends (who never dated) unexpectedly reunite on the way to the enchanted world of Gambler’s Folly, sparks fly and a full-blown romance blooms. Will they seize this second chance at a happily-ever-after, or will doubts and fears snatch it away? On Gambler’s Folly, every love story is a gamble—and Fate always deals the final hand. A slow-burn friends-to-lovers tale full of heart, sensuality, and the series’ signature fantasy charm.

About the author
Mellie Miller first fell in love with writing in a high school creative writing class. Married to her one and only, Steve, they began their journey through life in 1976 and, after two children and many moves, she finally has the time to devote to this love. She mainly writes fantasy romance, often with a paranormal twist, though she also has a short book sharing her struggle with breast cancer. Mellie feels her background in music, martial arts (2nd-degree black belt), and Reiki gives her a broad palette to draw on for her character development. Many of her stories incorporate one or more of these talents. As a lover of fantasy, Mellie hopes the worlds and stories she creates will give others a bit of escape from the hectic world around us and offer hope for a happy outcome. She and her husband live in rural Georgia and share their lives with cats, dogs, and a flock of chickens. She also writes under the pen name Sultonna Nadine.

text:
He called me proud. Emily called him controlling. Eventually, he stopped discussing money with me.

Or so I thought.

That night, I walked into the bathroom and called him.

He answered immediately.

“You received it,” he said.

“Why are you sending me forty thousand dollars?”

“Because you have a chance to leave this relationship with your dignity intact.”

“What arrangement are you talking about?”

He sighed impatiently.

“Emily has been seeing someone else. His name is James. Their families have known each other for years, and he is the kind of man who can provide the future she deserves.”

My stomach tightened.

“Are you telling me your daughter is cheating on me?”

“I'm telling you that feelings are complicated. James has offered to marry her, and Emily has been considering it.”

I looked through the bathroom doorway at the woman sleeping in our bed.

“Then why hasn't she told me?”

“Because she doesn't want to hurt you.”

I nearly laughed.

“So your solution is to buy me?”

“My solution is to prevent a humiliating situation for everyone involved.”

I ended the call.

For the next hour, I sat on the bathroom floor, staring at the transfer notification. I wanted to wake Emily and demand answers, but I also wanted to know how much of what her father had said was true.

Eventually, I returned to bed.

She was awake.

“Who were you talking to?” she asked.

“Your father.”

Her expression changed immediately.

“What did he say?”

I showed her the messages.

She covered her mouth, and tears filled her eyes.

“I'm sorry,” she whispered.

Those two words hurt more than anything her father had said.

I asked whether she knew about the money.

She nodded.

“Dad told me he was going to offer you something to leave. I didn't know he would send that much.”

“And James?”

She looked away.

“James and I went on three dates before you and I got engaged. Our families wanted us together, but I didn't feel what I feel for you.”

“Then why is your father telling me you're considering marrying him?”

Emily began crying.

“Because James came back six months ago. He told my father he still wanted me, and Dad started putting pressure on me again. I told him I wasn't interested.”

“Did you tell James that?”

“Yes.”

“Have you seen him since?”

She hesitated.

That hesitation changed the entire conversation.

“Emily, have you seen him since?”

“Twice.”

“Were those business meetings?”

“The first time, yes. The second time, we had dinner.”

I stepped away from her.

She immediately explained that her father had arranged the dinner without telling her James would be there. She claimed she stayed because leaving would have caused a scene.

I asked whether James had tried to kiss her.

She shook her head.

Then she admitted he had held her hand under the table.

“And you let him?”

“I pulled away.”

“After how long?”

She couldn't answer.

I left the bedroom and slept on the sofa.

The following morning, Emily told me everything.

Apparently, James had promised her father that he would buy a house for the couple, pay off a family business loan, and support Emily's mother financially. Richard believed the arrangement would protect the family from financial difficulties.

Emily insisted she had rejected the proposal.

But when I asked why she hadn't told me about the dinner, she said she was afraid I would misunderstand.

I told her that hiding something because your partner might be upset was exactly how misunderstandings became betrayals.

For three days, we barely spoke.

Then James contacted me directly.

He asked to meet at a restaurant.

I went because I wanted to hear what kind of man was willing to negotiate another man's engagement.

James arrived in an expensive car, ordered coffee, and spoke calmly.

“I don't want to fight you,” he said. “Emily deserves to choose her own future.”

“Then why are you trying to marry her?”

“Because I love her.”

“Does she love you?”

He looked down at his cup.

“She loved me once.”

text:
Internal Weather

Some days are really good.

The sun seems to shine just for us.
Truth flows effortlessly,
words find their way home,
and the heart glows with warmth.

Yesterday was one of those days.

And then there are days like today.

I wake beneath a sky I don’t recognize.
My body feels heavy.
My hands forget how to hold things.
I spill stuff and trip over my own feet.

And somewhere along the way,
a storm begins to gather.

A conversation that should have been easy
becomes a series of misunderstandings.
Our frequencies seem mismatched.
Every word I offer in an attempt to clarify
only distorts the meaning further.

Like raindrops falling on newspaper,
trying to wash the newsprint clean,
only to leave the words illegible.

Nothing is particularly wrong.
And yet everything feels wrong.

An inexplicable sense of doom.
A coldness where yesterday there was warmth.
Shivers down my spine,
my skin prickling like an anxious cat
sensing a storm before it arrives.

So which day was real?

Yesterday’s sunshine?
Or today’s darkness?

Maybe both.
Or neither.

Feelings are real.
Only in that they exist. But don’t believe the stories they try to tell.

We don’t question happiness.
We bask in its warmth without demanding proof.
But suffering arrives,
and suddenly we need to interrogate it 
like some detective or prosecutor. 

We question our relationships,
our choices, our entire existence,
Like pain possesses some special authority
to reveal truths that happiness cannot.

But why should it?

Perhaps my body woke up exhausted.
Perhaps hormones shifted.
Perhaps the pressure in the atmosphere changed.
Perhaps a thousand invisible conditions
converged to produce this particular storm.

I have no fucking clue.
And I don’t need to.

Weather be just weathering.

Moisture gathers.
Pressure shifts.
Clouds collide.
Rain falls.

It happens.
And then it passes.

We don’t declare that we shall henceforth
wear rainboots for the rest of our lives
simply because it’s raining today.

Nor should we make permanent declarations
about our lives
based on temporary emotional conditions.

A forecast is not a prophecy.
And forecasts are often wrong.

The sky does not become damaged by a storm.
Nor does it become more complete
when the sun returns.

It just holds space for whatever happens to occur.

So today, I will lay low.

I will resist the urge to explain,
to defend,
to untangle every misunderstanding,
to assign meaning to every uncomfortable feeling.

I will try not to create consequences
that outlast the conditions that produced them.

I will allow myself to feel unwell
without making it someone else’s emergency.

Emotional stability
is not the ability to remain perpetually sunny.
It’s how we handle the bad weather when it inevitably comes.

Yesterday was beautiful.
Today is difficult.

Neither invalidates the other.

And underneath it all,
the sky remains.

So I wait.

Until the storm passes.
Until the newspaper dries.
Until the words become legible again.

And in the meantime,

We apologize for any internal weather-related damages.

Floodwater reached Broad Street at Lockwood in Charleston on Monday. The morning warning was cancelled, but moderate coastal flooding is forecast around Tuesday’s 9:06 a.m. and Wednesday’s 9:57 a.m. high tides.

The coastal flood warning for Charleston and coastal Colleton was cancelled at 10:29 a.m. Monday, 31 minutes before its scheduled end. That cancellation did not end the week’s tidal-flooding threat.

Strong onshore winds combined with exceptionally high astronomical tides to push water toward the coast, leaving coastal roads vulnerable even under sunny skies. Further flooding could disrupt the next two morning commutes, with flood-prone routes potentially impassable until water recedes.

Monday’s warning forecast 1–2 feet of saltwater inundation above ground along shorelines and tidal waterways in Charleston and coastal Colleton. That was a forecast, not a measured street-water depth. The available evidence documents street flooding but does not establish an observed Charleston Harbor peak, confirmed property damage or a verified tally of road closures.

Potentially major flooding was forecast for Monday morning; the evidence does not confirm that major flood stage was reached. Moderate flooding remains the forecast for Tuesday and Wednesday mornings.

Tuesday, October 27’s high tide is at 9:06 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time. Wednesday, October 28’s is at 9:57 a.m. Charleston offers TIDEeye and a city flood-road-closure resource for checking routes. Current road conditions, rather than the end of Monday’s warning, should guide commute decisions.

#CharlestonFlooding #CoastalFlooding

DES MOINES, Iowa – Iowa Democrats are once again scraping the bottom of the barrel, digging up a nearly decade-old video of Joe Mitchell from when he was a 19-year-old college kid at Drake University in 2017. 

In the clip, a clearly intoxicated Mitchell can be heard making rambling comments typical of late-night dorm activities, talking about girls, joking around with friends, and saying some over-the-top things no sober adult would stand by.

Watch the Full Video Here:

A deceitful woman who was friends with Mitchell in college reportedly came forward with the video to the Daily Mail, saying that voters deserved “the full picture” of the candidate they were electing. 

Mitchell has already owned it and pointed out the obvious, in that he was 19, in college, and has grown up since then. Yet Democratic operatives and the Iowa Democratic Party are pushing the video hard as if it’s some kind of smoking gun, complete with press releases and social media pile-ons in the final days of a competitive race. 

This is the kind of cheap, desperate politics that shows just how little substance Democrats have left to offer Iowa voters. Instead of debating Mitchell’s record, his endorsement from President Trump, or his ideas for the 2nd District, they’re hoping that voters forget that virtually every young person says and does dumb things when they’re drunk in college, especially young Iowans. 

The selective outrage and character assassination directed at a young White man who’s built a business, served his community, and stepped up to run for office reeks of the same tired playbook Democrats always pull when they can’t win on the issues. Iowans deserve better than these cheap, shameful tactics.

But regulators acted swiftly to crack down on the company’s rivals.

Gov. Katie Hobbs and Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes have publicly pursued unlicensed gambling operators, naming firms they say are operating illegally and successfully pressuring some to exit the state.

Meanwhile, the Democrats kept quiet about a 2024 effort to shut down Virtual Gaming Worlds, an Australia-based company that has donated handsomely to officials on both sides of the aisle. That includes campaign contributions totaling $200,000, given to groups supporting Hobbs and Mayes.

The company’s operations in Arizona have continued.

Virtual Gaming Worlds, owned by Australian billionaire Laurence Escalante and better known by the acronym VGW, has embarked on a seven-figure political influence campaign across the U.S. this year as regulators push back against its online platforms.

As they benefit from VGW's campaign funds, Hobbs and Mayes have offered no clear explanation for why Arizona regulators appeared to treat the company differently from its peers.

Hobbs' office oversees the Arizona Department of Gaming, which handles licensing and investigates reports of illegal activity. Mayes' office has the power to prosecute and advises the agency on legal matters. Spokespersons for the two Democrats have pointed to jurisdictional challenges and the complexity of financial crimes or cryptocurrency. Mayes also highlighted a lack of resources to pursue complex cases.

Their offices on Oct. 22 again offered limited statements that did not address why the Gaming Department's disciplinary action against VGW was kept behind closed doors, while similar cases played out in public.

text:
A few days ago, @PittrpatterDon, 73, of Gilbert, Arizona, sent me something that humbled me. He wrote it himself, and he gave me permission to share it:

"While serving a senior mission at the Mormon Battalion, I began wrestling with back pain that grew sharp and insistent. One night, scrolling on X for both inspiration and distraction among fellow Latter-day Saints, I came across a post from @ALScyborg. Brad Smith lives with ALS. He cannot move his body, cannot speak, and relies on a ventilator. Yet through a Neuralink implant he types with his mind, edits videos, runs a podcast, and continues to teach, encourage, and serve. In that moment my own pain and problems were quickly brought into perspective.

What struck me was not only the severity of his limitations, but the way he magnified the abilities that remained. He did not wait for restoration; he worked with what he had. That example stayed with me. I began to ask how I might better serve within my own limitations—pain that limited mobility and energy, yet left my mind and voice intact. Soon I found myself using Grok to help shape lyrics, then Suno to turn those words into songs meant to lift sisters who were struggling with depression, anxiety, and homesickness. The technology became a tool for service rather than a distraction from my discomfort.

I have come to see that my limitations do not merely restrict me; they point me more clearly toward the Savior. They remind me that this body is temporary and that the hope of resurrection and restoration is not abstract. Brad will continue on the path of diminishment, and so will I, until both of us are gathered, surrounded by love and life, in the world to come. Until then, the work is the same: to seek a fuller measure of gratitude for what remains, and to keep looking to the One who offers living water and the bread of life.

The pain has not disappeared. I completed my mission, and the sisters still face hard days. Brad's body continues to fail. Yet in each case the response that matters most is the same—turning toward Christ, using whatever strength is left to bless others, and trusting that the restoration He promises will one day make all things whole."

More than 300 of Don's songs were played for sister missionaries, and many of them stayed on their missions because of his music. Don, you blessed those sisters, and you blessed me. None of us knows whose life we're touching.

Listen to his song: https://t.co/z7Y6x6xvIX 🎶

text:
To survive an overt military or fascist assault by a totalitarian state, the organization must synthesize the most ruthless, adaptive, and successful strategies of asymmetric warfare in human history.
By fusing the tactical innovations of historical insurgencies—ranging from the Americas to Southeast Asia—the Pan-African super-group transforms into an un-killable, self-replicating machine of total resistance.
Here is the ultimate blueprint for survival and victory under total state terror.

Phase I: Geopolitical Shock & Decapitation Insulation

Before firing a shot, the organization weaponizes the psychological and structural tactics of the early Conquistadors and the Haitian Revolution to paralyze the state apparatus.
                  [ FASCIST TOTALITARIAN STATE ATTACK ]
                                    │
         ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                     ▼
[ INTERNAL COGNITIVE SHOCK ]                         [ EXTERNAL DIPLOMATIC BLOCK ]
(Pizarro / Cortes Strategy)                          (Haitian Revolution Strategy)
 ├── High-Value Target Capture                        ├── Diaspora Alliances
 └── Internal Fracturing of Regime                    └── Scorched-Earth Economic Boycotts

1. The Shock Decapitation (The Pizarro & Cortes Strategy)

Francisco Pizarro (Incas) and Hernán Cortés (Aztecs) defeated vast empires by identifying the extreme centralization of their enemies, capturing their leaders (Atahualpa and Montezuma), and using local alliances to turn the empires against themselves.
• Exploiting Regime Rifts: The organization uses its deep intelligence network to find fracturing lines within the ruling fascist elite (e.g., rivalries between the military, corporate donors, and political factions).
• Targeted Leadership Capture: Instead of fighting the army, specialized underground commandos execute lightning-fast, deniable operations to capture or neutralize key regime architects, corporate backers, and propaganda masters. By removing the "brains" of the fascist state, the regime is thrown into chaotic infighting.
• The "Tlaxcalan" Alliance: Just as Cortés used the Tlaxcalans to destroy the Aztecs, the group forms deep alliances with other oppressed domestic demographics, creating a unified, multi-front civil war that forces the military to scatter its forces.

2. The Global Scorched-Earth (The Haitian Revolution Strategy)

Toussaint Louverture and Jean-Jacques Dessalines defeated global superpowers (France, Britain, Spain) by pairing unyielding physical brutality with a refusal to allow the enemy to live off the land.
• Sovereign Destruction of State Assets: If the military invades a Black urban or agricultural hub, the organization triggers an absolute scorched-earth protocol. Key supply lines, corporate infrastructure, and energy grids tied to the regime are systematically sabotaged. The state finds nothing but a resource-draining desert.
• International Geopolitical Blackmail: The Haitians successfully played global empires against each other. The organization leverages its global branches to offer strategic economic and intelligence assets to foreign rivals of the U.S. government, triggering international military blockades and starving the domestic regime of trade.

Phase II: The Ghost Theater (Asymmetric Defense)

When the military deploys heavy armor and aerial dominance, the organization vanishes into the terrain, combining the strategies of the Viet Cong and the Chichimeca people.
                    [ STRATEGIC MILITARY WITHDRAWAL ]
                                    │
          ┌─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┐
          ▼                                                   ▼
[ SUBTERRANEAN URBAN/RURAL FORTRESS ]               [ HYPER-MOBILE AMBUSH WARFARE ]
(Viet Cong Tunnel Networks)                        (Chichimeca Raid Tactics)
 ├── Concealed Hydroponic Food Production            ├── Complete Disappearance Post-Strike
 └── Zero-Signature Ammunition Depots               └── Poisoning of Enemy Logistics/Morale

1. The Subterranean Iron Grid (The Viet Cong Strategy)

The Viet Cong neutralized American air superiority, artillery, and technological dominance through the construction of hyper-complex, deeply layered underground systems like the Củ Chi tunnels.
• The Underground City Network: Beneath the agricultural land trusts and urban centers, the organization constructs multi-tiered, hardened tunnel complexes. These networks house command centers, factories for manufacturing defensive gear, hospitals, and concealed hydroponic food hubs.
• Zero-Signature Warfare: Troops move, sleep, and supply themselves entirely underground. Thermal imaging and satellite surveillance become useless. Military forces entering these zones are lured into carefully constructed, booby-trapped kill zones where heavy armor cannot maneuver, forcing the military into bloody, close-quarters infantry combat where they lose their technological advantage.

2. Hyper-Mobile Ghost Raids (The Chichimeca Strategy)

In the 16th-century Chichimeca War, nomadic indigenous tribes completely defeated the Spanish military by refusing to hold fixed positions, attacking silver supply trains, and vanishing into the arid terrain.
• Striking the Tendons: The organization’s security wing completely abandons uniforms and traditional military formations. Operating as "citizens by day, partisans by night," they use extreme mobility to strike the regime's weak points—fuel depots, communication towers, and troop transport lines.
• The Ghost Disappearance: The security units never stand and fight. They execute a 60-second ambush and instantly melt back into the civilian population or subterranean tunnels. The occupying military is left policing an apparently peaceful populace, shattering troop morale through permanent paranoia.

Phase III: The Shadow State (The Yugoslav Partisan Model)

To ensure the fascist regime cannot simply wait out the insurgency, the group implements the ultimate model of institutional resistance: Josip Broz Tito’s Yugoslav Partisans, the most effective anti-Nazi resistance movement in WWII.
                       [ THE SHADOW EMBED ]
                                │
         ┌──────────────────────┴──────────────────────┐
         ▼                                             ▼
[ LIBERATED PARALLEL TERRITORIES ]            [ TOTAL COGNITIVE INFILTRATION ]
(Yugoslav Partisan Model)                     (The "Invisible Citizen" Network)
 ├── Autonomous Courts & Laws                  ├── In-House Military Intelligence
 └── Total Community Self-Governance           └── Systematic Sabotage from Within

1. The Liberated Mobile Republic

Tito’s partisans didn't just hide; they actively built functioning democratic territories within occupied Europe, creating a parallel government that out-administered the fascists.
• Sovereign Law and Order: Within its spheres of influence, the organization establishes its own underground courts, security protocols, and economic trade ledgers. If the state infrastructure collapses or turns predatory, the community relies entirely on the organization for stability.
• The Universal Draft of Labor: Every single person in the community is given an underground role. If you are a cook, you feed the cadres; if you are a mechanic, you maintain the ghost logistics fleet; if you are a doctor, you run the underground clinics.

2. Total Cognitive Infiltration

• The Silent Inside Sabotage: Clean-record members systematically enlist in the regime’s National Guard, police forces, and logistical command centers.
• The Intelligence Shield: Every military plan, raid schedule, and undercover operative identity is intercepted by the group before it can be executed. When the fascist regime strikes, they hit empty buildings, while their own supply trucks systematically experience unexplained mechanical breakdowns and lost shipments.

Summary of Victory Condition

By combining these historical doctrines, the organization achieves an asymmetric paradox. The totalitarian regime discovers that the more military force it uses, the faster it destroys its own economy and stability. The regime is forced into a prolonged, resource-draining nightmare against an invisible enemy that controls the underground, holds the absolute loyalty of the population, and systematically dismantles the state from the inside out until the fascist apparatus collapses under its own weight.

Wisconsin Success Story: Isaac Howard, 2025 Hobey Baker Award

https://t.co/7pn8gsYdJj

-

By Matt Carey, Contributor, 04/22/25, 9:45AM CDT

Heart of a Lion

On April 11, 2025, Isaac ‘Ike’ Howard of Hudson, Wisconsin became the 45th Hobey Baker Award winner. Ike is the fourth Hobey winner that grew up in Wisconsin. In 1989 Lane MacDonald was the first, Will Butcher was second in 2017, and Cole Caufield third in 2021.

Since 1981 the Hobey Baker Award has been bestowed annually to the most outstanding college player. In addition to exceptional hockey skills, the Hobey recipient must demonstrate integrity, sportsmanship and strength of character.

The award is named after Hobart ‘Hobey’ Baker who played hockey and football for Princeton from 1910-14. Hobey is the first American to be inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in Toronto, and is the only person inducted in both the College Football and US Hockey Hall of Fames. Hobey Baker died on December 21, 1918, at age 26 in a plane crash while serving in the U.S. Army during World War I.

According to Ike’s father, Tony, Ike’s initiation into hockey came early. “He started playing in diapers! He watched his two older brothers, and he was raring to go. He wanted to follow his brothers. They started with knee hockey.”

As a little boy, Ike tagged along with his older brothers to the ice rink. Tony coached, so Ike would get on ice and practice with the older kids. The extra ice time was beneficial for Ike’s skill development. Ike’s mom, Crystal, viewed Ike’s extra ice through a paradigm of a mom with four young children. “With Tony coaching it was like having a built-in babysitter!”

Even as a young kid, Ike’s work ethic was off the charts. Ike’s mom said, “He was a hockey fanatic. He would come home after practice and shoot pucks. He loved it. He always had a different gear. We didn’t do anything different with him compared to the others (three brothers). It was just inside him”.

Ike displayed exceptional hockey skills at an early age. Ike’s dad commented, “He was ahead of the game at mites. At squirts he was leaps and bounds ahead.” Crystal and Tony could see Ike was an extraordinary player. But they weren’t certain how good.

At age 9 or 10 Ike’s potential was illuminated. According to Ike’s mom, “We knew he had a little extra to him. We didn’t know how good; we thought he was good for Hudson. It wasn’t until someone in Minnesota saw him and asked him to try out for Brick. I think it was in Edina. Tony calls and tells me he is one of the best. He made the team.”

Ike remained in Hudson for the next several years and received advanced training in the nearby suburbs. In 9th grade Ike made a bold move by leaving home for Shattuck. Ike’s mom stated, “It was a hard decision to have our 14-year-old move out and go to boarding school. But looking back it was the best decision.”

Ike thrived at Shattuck, tallying approximately 150 points in two seasons. Scouts from colleges and USA Hockey took notice. After two years at Shattuck, Ike joined USA Hockey’s National Team Development Program (NTDP), and he committed to the UMD Bulldogs. Ike continued his offensive prowess on the national stage by leading his NTDP team in scoring.

Following two seasons with NTDP, Ike was selected by the Tampa Bay Lightning in the first round of the 2022 NHL draft. Two months after the NHL draft, Ike started his freshman season with UMD. Ike had six goals and eleven assists in 35 games with the Bulldogs.

After his freshman year, Ike needed a new lease on life, so he made the decision to transfer. He decided to play for a familiar face. Adam Nightingale was Ike’s coach at NTDP, and he was the new head coach at Michigan State (MSU). Ike and Coach Nightingale are on the same wavelength. Ike found his home with the Spartans.

Ike moved east and started school at MSU for his sophomore season. Before the hockey season started, the medical staff at MSU reviewed Ike’s medical records. The medical records indicated abnormalities in his heart. MSU’s medical staff ordered additional tests.

Ike’s mom shared, “He was diagnosed with a heart condition. It was flagged when he went to the draft. Cardiologists said it could be monitored. Doctors at Michigan State wanted to do more tests. We were on a Zoom call, and they told us he had Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome, and he needed to have surgery. The surgery was successful. They fixed his heart. The cardiologist said this was a career ending surgery 10 years ago. It puts things in perspective. It can all go away. A new set of doctors saved his life. Everything happens for a reason. You have to be grateful.”

A person’s character surfaces during tense moments in life. Ike had difficulty walking for 10 days after the surgery. He didn’t wallow in self-pity. He wasn’t a victim. Ike remained positive, focused, and strong willed. He had a goal to accomplish. He needed to recover, get back on the ice, and be the best college hockey player. And that’s what he did!

Following heart surgery, by mid-season Ike was firing on all cylinders. In late December he joined Team USA for the World Juniors. Ike paved the way for a gold medal. He scored two goals in the gold medal game and was named the U.S. Player of the Game. Ike finished the season by helping MSU win a Big Ten championship while leading the team in points.

Ike returned for a spectacular second season at MSU that was culminated by winning the 2025 Hobey Baker Award. He led the Spartans to their first ever back-to-back Big Ten championship after scoring a dramatic double OT goal against Ohio State. Ike also led MSU in points for a second straight season and was named Big Ten MVP.

“As a young boy he knew what he wanted. His biggest asset is his compete level. He is the ultimate competitor and a guy you want on your team. His work ethic is second to none and he makes others better. I am very proud of him.” Mark Strobel, Ike’s squirt coach, former UW Badgers assistant coach and player

Let’s hear from Isaac Howard!

Congratulations on winning the Hobey Baker Award. Thank you!

What were your emotions hearing your name announced as the Hobey winner? It was surreal. Such a cool moment. I had my family, coach (MSU Head Coach), and people that mean a lot to share it with. I knew the other candidates well, we won a gold medal in Sweden, and they are great players. It was humbling.

Was this a similar feeling you had at the NHL draft? Yeah, definitely. The Hobey was even bigger. It felt bigger in that moment.

Who were the most influential people in your life growing up? Definitely my family. We have a tight family. My parents are blue collar people, and they worked to make my dream a reality. My brothers…hanging out with them competing and being knuckleheads.

Did your family attend the Hobey Award and NHL draft? Everyone was there for both.

What did it mean to you to have your family at the Hobey and NHL draft? It is super special. It is great to have them there for big moments in life. It is fun to be around them. We really have fun together.

What are your favorite memories of youth hockey? I loved playing pond hockey in the winter. Going to my brothers’ practices. I loved playing at Shattuck. I remember growing up in Hudson and winning the state championship.

What are some of your favorite memories of playing with NTDP? Playing my first USHL game. The international tournaments. Seeing the world; Germany, Sweden, Switzerland. Putting the USA jersey on. It is special putting the USA jersey on. It always is. Winning the gold medal last year capped everything off.

Your game is clicking at MSU…what do you attribute the success to? I think the resources here. Everything they offer I take advantage of. Extra ice, training sessions, film sessions, and the training staff is so good.

Did having heart surgery impact your perspective on life? Definitely has. It gave me a glimpse of what life could be without hockey. It makes me more grounded and appreciate the opportunities. Take advantage of the opportunities.

Do you feel attending MSU was meant to be or a divine intervention? Yes, I think it was. This place is special to me. The care they have for me is more than hockey. They look at me as a human. I will be forever grateful that the medical staff took the extra tests on my heart.

You are returning to MSU…what part of your game do you want to improve? I want to take on a leadership role. Help grow my leadership with the young players coming in. On the ice to get stronger, faster, better with the puck and without the puck.

Where is your dream vacation? Maybe Hawaii. Surfing, deep-sea fishing, the beach.

Pickup truck or sports car? Sports car. Pink and light blue Lamborghini!

Chocolate cake, brownie, or apple pie? Chocolate cake.

Is there a book you’ve read that positively influenced you? Mind Gym. Alex Rodriguez is the author. It’s a book on the mental side. Believing in yourself. I recommend that book. It can help beyond athletics. Your mental performance impacts your physical performance.

What advice do you have for kids that want to play after HS? Focus on yourself and what you need to do. You have to do stuff that makes you uncomfortable. There are sacrifices you need to make.

Ike’s parents, Tony and Crystal, currently live in Hudson, Wisconsin. The high school sweethearts from St. Paul have four sons, each separated by a couple years. Anthony is the oldest, followed by Mason, Ike, and Eli. Crystal continues to be a key volunteer for the hockey program in Hudson even after her children have graduated.

Ike’s mental toughness, work ethic, and positivity is inspirational!

-
*(via Matt Carey, WisconsinPrepHockey).

PREVIEW: Oilers vs. Red Wings

https://t.co/bTHM24YBVJ

The Oilers continue their five-game homestand at Rogers Place against the Red Wings on Monday
-

"I thought we were going to be right," Head Coach Mike Babcock said. "We weren't, but give them credit. They got ready, they came in here, they're on a road trip, they got prepared, and they played harder and faster for longer than we did. Better defensively, better offensively, just better."

"I loved our last game. I thought it was great," he said. "We played a really good team, and I thought we were ultra competitive. I thought they took over at times. I thought we took over at times.  And my hope for today was that we were going to match that level of compete and then raise it. We didn't do any of that, so that's a step back.  Tonight wasn't good enough, period."

RED WINGS TEAM SCOPE

Like the Oilers, the Red Wings are just off having a six-game point streak snapped in their final trip to the Scotiabank Saddledome on Saturday, falling 4-1 to the Calgary Flames as they look to close out their four-game Western road trip in Edmonton on Monday with a victory to take home.

To keep the theme going, Head Coach Todd McLellan said the Flames were better in multiple areas, especially on special teams, where Calgary scored on both of their power plays and stopped Detroit on both of their chances on the man advantage.

Both the coach & players cited it as one of their poorer efforts of the season.

“I just never really felt like we got traction in the game,” forward Andrew Copp said. “We had some good shifts, maybe a couple good minutes at a time, but never really kind of fully got in control of the game and shift after shift where we were doing all the right things. So, some little mistakes that kind of cost us shifts where it was a good shift, then something happens and all of a sudden, we’re in our own zone, or we’re taking a penalty."

"It wasn’t our best night, for sure. We have one more game to salvage the road trip.”

Forward Alex DeBrincat, who signed a seven-year extension at an AAV of $13 million earlier this month, leads the Red Wings in scoring with six goals 12 points ahead of Lucas Raymond (3G, 6A) and former Oilers forward Viktor Arvidsson (4G, 4A).

Goaltender John Gibson made 22 saves in the loss to the Flames and owns a 3-4-0 record, a .867 save percentage and 3.44 goals-against average,

BY THE NUMBERS

The Oilers have lost in regulation just once in their last nine meetings with the Red Wings, going 6-1-2 and outscoring them 38-26.

The Oilers haven't lost in regulation in six straight home meetings with the Red Wings, going 4-0-2 and outscoring them 27-17. 

Last season, the Oilers rebounded from a 4-2 loss in Detroit on Oct. 19 with a 4-1 win at Rogers Place on December 11, levelling the season series at a game apiece.

Connor McDavid led all Edmonton scorers in the season series with four assists, collecting all four in the Dec. 11 game while Zach Hyman (3G) and Leon Draisaitl (1G, 2A) each snagged three points.

McDavid's 33 points mark one of the best starts to a season in NHL history and Oilers history.

He has 33 points on 48 Oilers goals this season. His 68.8% of team goals involved would be the highest in a season in NHL history, breaking his own record (57.4 percent) from 2020-21.

The Oilers are scoring an NHL-high 4.36 goals per game this season, but they rank 27th in goals against per game (3.55).

McDavid & Draisaitl are just 5 goals combined on short of tying the Red Wings ‘Production Line’ duo Gordie Howe & Alex Delvecchio (560) for the 4th-most goals combined on by a teammate duo in NHL history.

McDavid (33), Draisaitl (23) & Evan Bouchard (21) each have 20+ points through 11 games this season. There have only been 6 teams to feature 3+ players with 20+ points through 11 games of a season prior to 2026-27:

2026-27 Oilers 
2005-06 Senators 
1995-96 Penguins 
1988-89 Penguins 
1984-85 Islanders 
1983-84 Nordiques 
1980-81 Kings 

The Red Wings line of Alex DeBrincat, Emmitt Finnie & Michael Brandsegg-Nygard has been dominant this season with the Red Wings outscoring opponents 8-1 with them on the ice.

By Jamie Umbach Edmonton Oilers
-

The Edmonton Oilers look to bounce back from Saturday's defeat as they continue their five-game homestand at Rogers Place with a visit from the Detroit Red Wings on Monday.

Goaltender Tristan Jarry will make his second straight start, while forward Isaac Howard will return to the lineup on the four line next to Trent Frederic and Colton Dach in place of Max Jones, who'll be an extra forward alongside Filip Hallander.

After being a healthy scratch on Saturday, Trent Frederic will return to the fourth line as he works to regain his confidence and make an impact, scoring one goal and averaging 9:40 of ice time over 10 games this season.

"Being harder on the puck is more of the message," Frederic said. "When I have the puck, be hard on it, win my battles, and just play physical and get some heavy hits."

Mattias Ekholm was on the ice for the morning skate but remains out with an upper-body injury, along with Jason Dickinson, as both skaters hope to be available for the Oilers on their upcoming three-game road trip to New York starting this weekend.

After the Oilers were hit for seven goals in a complete effort from the Maple Leafs in Saturday's 7-2 loss on home ice, putting an end to their three-game win streak, Head Coach Mike Babcock wants to see his side respond by quickly getting back to playing to their identity and building out their roles

Despite being 8-2-1 this season, there's still plenty for them to work on to establish themselves as a four-line team and produce more at even strength beyond their top line and first-unit power play, which has accounted for a large part of their scoring.

"We're a work in progress," Babcock said. "I thought it was going pretty good, and then I didn't like it as much. So the bottom line is we just got to keep plugging away. Just like in life, in the National Hockey League, you want your ups to be longer than your downs. And when you're having a down, you want to get it turned around in a hurry, so that's our focus."

FIRST STAR – LEON DRAISAITL, C, EDMONTON OILERS

Draisaitl scored twice in each of his three appearances to register a League-best six goals and place second with nine points (6-3—9) as the Oilers (8-2-1, 17 points) earned a pair of wins to move into first place in the Pacific Division. Draisaitl, who also led the NHL with five power-play goals (three more than the next-closest player), found the back of the net twice on the man-advantage as part of a 4-3 overtime victory against the Minnesota Wild Oct. 20. He then posted 2-3—5, his eighth career five-point performance, in a 6-5 shootout triumph versus the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes Oct. 22. Draisaitl closed the week with both Edmonton goals, his sixth straight contest with at least one tally (Oct. 13-24: 9-5—14), in a 7-2 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs Oct. 24. The 30-year-old Draisaitl, who claimed the Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophy in 2024-25 and has four 50-goal seasons to his credit, ranks second in the League with 12 goals and 23 points through 11 total games in 2026-27 (12-11—23). He also sits among this season’s leaders in power-play goals (1st; 6), power-play points (t-4th; 8), plus/minus (6th; +12), assists (t-8th; 11) and shots on goal (9th; 43). Draisaitl will look to extend his overall and multi-goal streaks tonight when the Oilers play host to the Detroit Red Wings on Monday Night Hockey on Sportsnet+ (9:30 p.m. ET/7:30 p.m. MT).

text:
This seems like a good place to explain that the best way to handle this need for a tribe is found in the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. I had Grok help me pull this together.

In Latter-day Saint (LDS/Mormon) theology, the deep human drive for tribal belonging and a homeland is fulfilled at the highest level by recognizing God as our literal Heavenly Father and by actively building Zion as a covenant community of the pure in heart.

This is not a secondary social program but the core of the plan of salvation. Humans are seen as pack animals with real needs for identity, loyalty, mutual defense, and place; those needs are redirected and elevated rather than suppressed or left to ethnic/nationalist outlets that can turn destructive.

Heavenly Father as the Primary Father and Tribe
LDS doctrine teaches that all people are the literal spirit children of Heavenly Parents. Before birth, spirits lived with God in a premortal existence; each person is a beloved son or daughter with divine nature and destiny. The Family: A Proclamation to the World states this directly: every human being is a spirit son or daughter of heavenly parents.

This creates the ultimate family identity. Earthly tribes, nations, and ethnic groups are secondary and temporary. The first and lasting “tribe” is the family of God—all people as brothers and sisters under the same Father. Christ is the Firstborn in the spirit, and through covenants, people can be born again into a closer relationship with Him and the Father. This identity is not abstract; it is reinforced by ordinances, temple work (which seals families eternally), and the constant teaching that “I am a child of God.”

It addresses the belonging instinct by rooting it in an eternal, non-contingent source. No political boundary or demographic change can revoke it. At the same time, it undercuts purely exclusionary tribalism: everyone is already in the family, and the work is to help more people enter the covenant path.

Patriarchal Blessings and the House of Israel
Within that universal family, LDS practice provides a specific tribal identity. Worthy members receive a patriarchal blessing that declares their lineage in the house of Israel—usually the tribe of Ephraim or Manasseh for many, or another of the twelve tribes. This is by bloodline or by adoption through baptism. It makes the person an heir to the Abrahamic covenant with its promises of posterity, priesthood, and land.

This satisfies the desire for a named tribe and inheritance without requiring exclusive ethnic purity. Members become part of the gathering of Israel, which modern Church leaders describe as happening primarily in the nations and lands where people already live, while still looking toward a central New Jerusalem.

Building Zion as the Earthly Homeland and Community
Zion is the practical and spiritual expression of this tribal need. Scripture defines it as “the pure in heart” (Doctrine and Covenants 97:21). The classic description is of Enoch’s people: “the Lord called his people Zion, because they were of one heart and one mind, and dwelt in righteousness; and there was no poor among them” (Moses 7:18). That city was eventually taken up into heaven.

In the latter days, building Zion means:

Creating stakes of Zion as gathering places and refuges.
Living in local wards and branches that function as tight communities of mutual support, ordinances, welfare, and shared purpose.
Working toward unity of heart and mind, care for the poor, and righteousness so that the society itself becomes Zion.
Preparing physical places (historically Independence, Missouri, and the Mountain West; now worldwide stakes and temples) where the pure in heart can dwell in safety and order.
Early Latter-day Saints sacrificed to gather and build cities, temples, and a cooperative society precisely because they saw this as establishing the Kingdom of God—an earthly homeland for God’s children. Today the emphasis is on building Zion in one’s own nation and community while remaining part of a global covenant people. The result is high levels of social cohesion, frequent interaction outside formal meetings, and a sense of belonging that surveys have shown is unusually strong among members.

Why This Is Presented as the Superior Handling of the Tribal Drive
From the LDS view, ethnic or purely national tribes can meet short-term belonging needs but tend toward conflict, exclusion, and eventual dissolution when demographics or power shift. The divine family plus Zion offers:

An identity that is eternal and cannot be taken by politics or migration.
A community ordered by covenants, priesthood, and mutual care rather than race or citizenship alone.
A homeland that is both spiritual (pure hearts anywhere) and physical (stakes, temples, and eventually millennial Zion/New Jerusalem).
A purpose that channels the pack instinct into building something righteous and durable instead of reactive nationalism or radicalization.
The local ward becomes the everyday “tribe,” the stake the larger homeland structure, the house of Israel the ancestral tribe, and the family of God the eternal one. Failure to provide this higher belonging, the theology implies, leaves the instinct unsatisfied and more likely to turn toward the very conflicts the original post warned about.

text:
Humans are a pack animal. 

This may be hard to understand if you are evangelical and think the book of genesis is literal rather than allegorical, but humans are a pack animal. 

What this means is that the human desire for the acceptance and support of a tribe is as fundamental as the desire for food, for air, for water, for sex, for sunlight, for love.

If you tell young men that they cannot have a tribe, they're not going to accept that.

Ever. 

Especially if you tell that only to the young men of one tribe in particular. They're going to wonder why everybody gets to have a tribe and they don't. 

And they're eventually going to decide that you are the enemy. 

Because you are. Anyone who stands between young men and what they need for a healthy, fulfilled life is their enemy. 

That includes you. 

And if you manage to convince them that god doesn't want them to have a tribe, it will also include god. 

The more you push back against their healthy and natural desire for a tribe, a homeland, and a birthright, the more they will hate you, and the more exclusive their definition of that tribe will become. 

There is no way you can stop this. The only thing you can control is how far they have to go, how radical they have to become, in order to get it. 

Because this can go all the way from enforcing immigration law, and shutting down corrupt visa programs right now, to gangs of young White men in balaclavas with Ar15s going door to door ten years from now. 

We have to do something about the 14th amendment. I don't care if that makes you uncomfortable or unhappy. It's not a choice. The constitution exists to serve Americans, not the other way around. If that sentence confuses you, read the first paragraph of the constitution. 

If we do not, young men of the future, the same little boys who are being radicalized right now by your malicious indifference, will treat a piece of paper that says they cannot have a homeland the way they would treat a piece of paper that says that can't eat food, or a piece of paper that says they can't own a home, or have a wife and children. 

You may think that you offer them a tribe in the form of the universal kingdom of god, the community of all believers, but that's just a word game and you know it, which is why you are so defensive about the whole thing. 

Where was the universal community of believers when these young men needed help? When they needed not just the surface appearance of a tribe, but someone to do the things that tribes actually do for younger generations they care about?

The pack serves a concrete set of functions in the life cycle of the human species, and you cannot perform those functions with a cardboard cutout. 

Young men are sick of religion that offers them responsibilities with no rights, lectures with no help, demands with no love or empathy. 

It's odd, in a way ironic, that, I, the man of zero faith, should have to be the one standing here telling self-styled religious leaders how they failed both their people and their god. 

But having no faith does give me one advantage. It frees me from the delusion that Jesus is a puppet that I can pull out of my pocket, slip over my right hand, move his mouth and make him say what I want. 

I used to wonder, as a child, what the phrase "taking the name of the lord in vain" actually meant. 

But I no longer wonder, because when I became a man, I looked around me and saw all these people who talk to god and somehow get told exactly what they want to hear. 

Then I understood that the key phrase here wasn't "in vain". It was "taking". Taking the name of god and using it as a tool for one's own goals. 

Joel, here, is sad that his friend is getting sent home. This personally inconveniences both him and his friend, which effects Joel in a way that young men being denied their birthright does not. 

So he finds an interpretation of scripture that says that god wants him, Joel Berry, to get his way, and that god wants all the young men who want a homeland and a birthright to go get fucked. 

I'm not terribly impressed.
