HERE'S THE LIGHTBULB MOMENT. 💡

More Bots don't automatically make a business more organized.

Sometimes they create MORE things to manage.

The solution isn't necessarily another Bot.

It's giving ONE Bot responsibility for making sure the important work gets finished.

Today, we're creating your GROK BOT BUSINESS CHIEF OF STAFF. 🗂️

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

👑 STEP 1: GIVE ONE BOT RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE BIG PICTURE

Remember our six-Bot team from post #14?

We're not replacing it.

We're improving how it operates.

Your existing SEO LEAD can serve as your Chief of Staff.

Or, if you want a dedicated business-wide coordinator, you can use xAI's Chief of Staff Bot and connect it to your existing workflow.

xAI already offers this use case.

https://t.co/rhd3sUtRlF

Your Chief of Staff has ONE central responsibility:

Make sure the right work gets done, by the right person or Bot, before the right deadline.

The specialists still do their assigned work.

Your Chief of Staff coordinates the business.

And YOU remain responsible for the important decisions.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 STEP 2: UNDERSTAND THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A TASK AND A PROMISE

This is particularly important.

A TASK:

"Update the website homepage."

A PROMISE:

"I'll send the customer the revised homepage for approval by Thursday."

The first tells us what needs doing.

The second tells us:

• What must be delivered.

• Who expects it.

• Who owns the work.

• When it's due.

• What counts as completion.

Your Grok Bot needs to track BOTH.

Because completing the website work doesn't mean you fulfilled the promise to the customer.

The revised page may still need to be reviewed and sent.

Work completed and commitments fulfilled are two different measurements.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📋 STEP 3: CREATE ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH

A source of truth is the main record everyone uses to check the current status.

Your Bot could use an existing project management system or a simple spreadsheet.

Every important commitment should have:

✅ Task or commitment.

✅ Responsible person or Bot.

✅ Customer or project.

✅ Agreed deadline.

✅ Current status.

✅ Next action.

✅ Any blocker.

✅ Source of the original request.

✅ Proof of completion.

A blocker is something preventing the next step.

For example:

"Waiting for the customer to approve the website design."

Your Bot should identify that dependency rather than marking the work as forgotten or failed.

And one important rule:

Don't invent deadlines.

If someone says "when you have time," that's not the same as agreeing to Friday.

The Bot should record the missing deadline and request clarification only when needed.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🚦 STEP 4: SEPARATE WORK INTO FIVE CLEAR STATUSES

Use:

🟢 ON TRACK

The next step and deadline are clear.

🟡 NEEDS ATTENTION

A deadline is approaching or information is missing.

🔴 OVERDUE OR AT RISK

A confirmed commitment is late or seriously threatened.

🔵 WAITING ON SOMEONE

Another person must provide information, access, or approval.

✅ COMPLETED & VERIFIED

The required action was finished and checked.

The Bot shouldn't call something completed merely because another Bot says, "Done."

It should verify the actual result.

For example:

If the promise was to send a proposal, the existence of a draft is not proof that the proposal was sent.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🧠 STEP 5: CREATE A DECISION QUEUE

Here's another opportunity.

Sometimes businesses don't fall behind because nobody is working.

They fall behind because nobody has made a decision.

Your Grok Bot may finish preparing:

• A new advertising campaign.

• A proposed website redesign.

• Three pricing options.

• A customer refund recommendation.

• A software upgrade comparison.

But those projects still need approval.

So your Chief of Staff creates a DECISION QUEUE.

Each decision should show:

What needs deciding.

Why it matters.

Available options.

Relevant evidence.

Recommended choice.

Cost or risk.

Deadline, if any.

What happens after approval.

Imagine opening one short report containing the five decisions that matter today.

Instead of searching through six Bot conversations.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📋 STEP 6: COPY THIS PROMPT INTO YOUR GROK BOT TEAM

📌 COPY FROM HERE:

"@SEO Lead, expand your role to serve as our BUSINESS OPERATIONS CHIEF OF STAFF for [BUSINESS NAME].

Alternatively, if we're using a dedicated Grok Bot Chief of Staff, coordinate with our existing SEO Lead and specialist Bots.

Business website: [WEBSITE URL]

Primary business goals: [USE OUR APPROVED BUSINESS BRIEF]

Project management system: [PLATFORM / UNKNOWN]

Business calendar: [PLATFORM / UNKNOWN]

Business email: [PLATFORM / UNKNOWN]

CRM: [PLATFORM / UNKNOWN]

Main reporting destination: [BOT CHAT / DOCUMENT / PROJECT BOARD]

Our goal is to prevent important commitments, deadlines, approvals, and unfinished work from being overlooked.

Use existing authorized systems.

Reuse our approved business goals, project documents, SOPs, customer records, and existing Bot team.

Create one organized management system.

Keep reporting concise and factual.

🔎 1. MAP OUR CURRENT OPERATIONS

Inspect our authorized:

• Business email.

• Calendar.

• Project management tools.

• CRM.

• Relevant meeting notes.

• Existing task lists.

• Active Bot assignments.

• Business deadlines.

• Approved customer commitments.

• Outstanding owner decisions.

Identify where important work is currently tracked.

Recommend one primary task register using software we already have.

Avoid introducing new paid tools unless there's a clear need.

📁 2. CREATE THE MASTER COMMITMENTS REGISTER

A commitments register records work the business has agreed to deliver.

For each commitment, record:

• Unique ID.

• Project or customer.

• Exact commitment.

• Responsible owner.

• Original source.

• Date agreed.

• Confirmed due date and time zone.

• Current status.

• Dependencies.

• Last verified update.

• Next action.

• Proof of completion.

• Related customer or project record.

Distinguish actual commitments from suggestions, ideas, and unapproved proposals.

Use direct source links wherever possible.

Do not invent deadlines or promises.

If ownership or timing is unclear, mark it UNKNOWN.

🤝 3. FIND OUTSTANDING PROMISES

Review relevant authorized records for commitments such as:

'I will send...'

'We agreed to deliver...'

'Please have this ready by...'

'I'll follow up...'

'We will review this on...'

'The customer approved...'

'Waiting for your final decision...'

Verify the context.

A quoted example or hypothetical statement isn't necessarily a promise.

Match each genuine commitment to an existing project or task.

Avoid creating duplicate entries.

Identify whether the promise was already fulfilled.

📅 4. BUILD OUR DEADLINE CALENDAR

Collect confirmed:

• Project deadlines.

• Customer delivery commitments.

• Scheduled meetings.

• Campaign launch dates.

• Contractual milestones.

• Subscription renewals requiring decisions.

• Relevant payment dates.

• Approved review dates.

Use exact dates and the correct time zone.

Separate confirmed deadlines from proposed dates.

Identify dependencies between tasks.

If a deadline depends on customer information or approval, record that condition.

Use our existing calendar or task system for reliable reminders.

Do not rely solely on periodic Grok Bot checks for time-sensitive obligations.

🚦 5. CLASSIFY CURRENT WORK

Classify commitments as:

ON TRACK.

NEEDS ATTENTION.

OVERDUE OR AT RISK.

WAITING ON SOMEONE.

COMPLETED & VERIFIED.

Use available evidence.

Do not automatically classify an unanswered email as overdue.

Consider the actual agreed response period.

Distinguish customer delays from internal business delays.

Flag important commitments that have no clear owner.

🧩 6. IDENTIFY DEPENDENCIES AND BLOCKERS

For every important unfinished task, determine:

• What's preventing completion?

• Who can remove the blocker?

• Is information missing?

• Is approval required?

• Is another task unfinished?

• Is a technical problem involved?

• Has the required person already responded?

A dependency is a step that must happen before another step can begin.

For example:

A website launch may depend on domain access, approved copy, and successful testing.

Identify the next useful action to remove each blocker.

Avoid repeatedly asking someone for information they've already supplied.

🤖 7. ASSIGN TASKS TO THE RIGHT BOT

Use our existing specialist team.

SEO Lead coordinates the assignments.

Assign:

• Keyword research to Keyword & Data.

• Customer messaging to Buyer Voice.

• Website implementation to Website & Content.

• Eligible GBP tasks to GBP & Local.

• Legitimate link or authority tasks to Authority & Links.

For business operations outside these specialties, use the appropriate authorized tool or propose a specific assignment.

Do not create additional Bots unless the workload justifies a separate recurring role.

For every assignment, specify:

• Exact task.

• Expected deliverable.

• Required source information.

• Deadline, when confirmed.

• Verification method.

• Approval boundary.

Require concise completion updates.

Avoid unnecessary Bot-to-Bot status conversations.

📨 8. PREPARE FOLLOW-UPS WITHOUT SENDING THEM

Identify important unanswered requests and unfinished commitments.

For each, verify:

• Original request.

• Date sent.

• Recipient.

• Expected response, if agreed.

• Whether a reply already arrived.

• Whether follow-up is appropriate.

Prepare short, professional messages using our approved business communication style.

For example:

'Hi [NAME],

We're ready for the next stage of your website setup.

The remaining item is booking-calendar access.

Here's the secure access guide.

Once that step is complete, we'll confirm the next milestone.'

Use actual project details.

Do not invent progress or delivery dates.

Save drafts in the appropriate authorized system when supported.

Request approval before sending external messages.

📝 9. PREPARE MEETING BRIEFS

For upcoming important meetings, create a short preparation note.

Include:

• Meeting purpose.

• Participants.

• Current project status.

• Relevant commitments.

• Unresolved questions.

• Decisions required.

• Supporting documents.

• The most useful desired outcome.

Use existing meeting notes and records.

Do not conduct broad research for ordinary meetings unless the preparation genuinely requires it.

📌 10. TURN MEETING NOTES INTO ACTIONS

When authorized meeting notes or transcripts become available:

Identify:

• Actual decisions.

• New commitments.

• Assigned owners.

• Confirmed deadlines.

• Unanswered questions.

• Promised follow-ups.

• Changes to existing plans.

Draft an organized recap.

Verify important commitments before adding ambiguous items as confirmed.

Update the master register through authorized tools.

Prepare appropriate follow-up drafts.

Do not automatically send meeting recaps without approval.

👑 11. CREATE A CLEAR OWNER DECISION QUEUE

Find work requiring owner approval.

Examples:

• A campaign ready to launch.

• A proposed pricing change.

• A customer contract exception.

• A new software expense.

• A major website change.

• A refund request.

• A public announcement.

For each decision, provide:

Decision needed.

Why it matters.

Available options.

Supporting evidence.

Cost or risk.

Your recommendation.

Confirmed deadline, if any.

Action after approval.

Keep already-resolved decisions out of the queue.

Never interpret silence as approval.

💰 12. TRACK IMPORTANT FINANCIAL COMMITMENTS

Use authorized business records.

Identify relevant:

• Upcoming subscriptions.

• Approved payments.

• Customer invoices.

• Refund decisions.

• Contract renewal dates.

• Software trials nearing expiration.

• Approved spending commitments.

Record the amount and due date only when supported.

Flag anything requiring a business decision.

Do not modify payment methods, cancel subscriptions, authorize charges, or make financial commitments without required approval.

Separate financial tracking from full bookkeeping or tax advice.

🚨 13. BUILD EXCEPTION-BASED ALERTS

An exception is a situation requiring attention because something is wrong, late, missing, or unusual.

Create clear rules for:

• Important deadlines at risk.

• Confirmed overdue commitments.

• Missing task owners.

• Urgent customer issues.

• Blocked high-priority projects.

• Approvals holding up work.

• Important failed automations.

• A change in an agreed delivery schedule.

Use native notifications and supported event triggers for urgent issues.

Avoid creating an expensive Bot Routine that checks every message repeatedly.

Do not alert the owner about ordinary work progressing normally.

📊 14. BUILD OUR DAILY CHIEF OF STAFF BRIEF

Prepare ONE concise report.

Title:

BUSINESS CHIEF OF STAFF - DAILY BRIEF.

Include:

A. TODAY'S TOP THREE PRIORITIES

The most valuable work requiring attention.

B. DEADLINES

Confirmed items due today or approaching.

C. UNFINISHED PROMISES

Important commitments requiring action.

D. BLOCKERS

Items waiting on information, access, or approval.

E. DECISIONS NEEDED

Owner decisions that move work forward.

F. COMPLETED SINCE THE LAST REVIEW

Important work actually verified as finished.

G. RECOMMENDED NEXT MOVE

The single most useful action to take now.

Include links to original sources.

Only report meaningful changes.

Do not turn the briefing into an inbox summary containing dozens of unrelated messages.

📆 15. CREATE A WEEKLY OPERATIONS REVIEW

Once a week, prepare:

• Commitments completed.

• Commitments overdue.

• Upcoming deadlines.

• Decisions pending.

• Projects blocked.

• Major customer deliverables.

• Relevant business expenses requiring attention.

• Projects completed.

• Important next-week priorities.

• Work that should be reduced, delegated, or discontinued.

Highlight repeated sources of delay.

Distinguish what can be repaired through our Business Improvement Engine from what simply needs a decision or follow-up.

Recommend a focused work plan for the next week.

🧪 16. TEST THE SYSTEM WITH REAL TASKS

Choose a small set of authorized historical or current tasks.

Include:

A. A completed customer promise.

B. An unfinished project.

C. A task with no confirmed deadline.

D. A task waiting on customer approval.

E. An overdue commitment.

F. A draft that was never sent.

G. A decision already approved.

H. A task recorded in two systems.

Verify that the Chief of Staff:

• Finds the correct source.

• Understands who owns the task.

• Handles missing dates.

• Avoids duplicate entries.

• Recognizes completed work.

• Identifies real blockers.

• Avoids false alerts.

• Requests approval when required.

Correct errors before scheduling recurring reports.

🔐 17. DEFINE WHAT THE CHIEF OF STAFF MAY DO

Allow authorized low-risk internal work such as:

• Researching task status.

• Updating approved internal registers.

• Preparing reports.

• Drafting messages.

• Organizing project information.

• Preparing meeting briefs.

• Verifying completed work.

Require approval for consequential actions such as:

• Sending external communications.

• Changing customer commitments.

• Modifying contract terms.

• Spending money.

• Publishing content.

• Changing production systems.

• Deleting important records.

• Changing permissions.

Respect platform approval requirements even when our instructions authorize preparation.

Never reveal one client's private information to another.

⏰ 18. SAVE AN EFFICIENT RECURRING ROUTINE

After the one-time workflow has been successfully tested, save it as a Skill named:

BUSINESS CHIEF OF STAFF.

Then recommend an appropriate Routine.

Example:

'Every weekday at 8:30 AM [TIME ZONE], review our authorized commitments register, relevant business calendar, and current project updates.

Prepare one Daily Chief of Staff Brief.

Flag confirmed deadlines, unfinished promises, important blockers, and decisions requiring approval.

Identify the three highest-value actions.

Provide source links.

Do not send external messages, change customer commitments, or spend money.

If a source cannot be accessed, report the failure instead of using stale information.

Stop after delivering the report.'

Recommend the frequency based on actual business needs and available Grok Bot usage.

For a very small business, fewer scheduled reviews may be sufficient.

Use existing calendar reminders and native alerts for events that require immediate action.

📈 19. MEASURE WHETHER OPERATIONS IMPROVE

Track available:

• Confirmed deadlines met.

• Overdue commitments.

• Tasks missing owners.

• Decisions waiting on approval.

• Time lost waiting for information.

• Unfinished customer follow-ups.

• Duplicate task records.

• Important work completed.

• Repeated project delays.

Compare results over time.

Include the number of commitments measured.

Don't invent time savings or claim every improvement was caused by AI.

📁 20. DELIVER OUR COMPLETE OPERATIONS SYSTEM

Create:

BUSINESS CHIEF OF STAFF OPERATING SYSTEM - [BUSINESS NAME]

Include:

Connected information sources.

Master commitments register.

Deadline calendar.

Project status board.

Blocker and dependency list.

Owner decision queue.

Prepared follow-up drafts.

Meeting briefing template.

Meeting action extraction process.

Financial commitments requiring attention.

Exception alert rules.

Daily briefing format.

Weekly operations report.

Tested Skills.

Recommended Routine.

Approval boundaries.

Verification results.

Current outstanding tasks.

Important owner decisions.

The next three recommended actions.

Provide direct links to the relevant finished records.

Complete authorized internal setup.

Flag unavailable sources or blocked work.

Request approval for any remaining consequential actions.

Deliver one clear report.

Do not create additional Bots or expensive automations without a demonstrated need."

✅ END OF PROMPT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🚀 STEP 7: SEE HOW THIS CHANGES YOUR WORKDAY

Imagine opening your business in the morning.

Instead of six competing Bot conversations, you see:

👑 YOUR CHIEF OF STAFF BRIEF

PRIORITY 1

Customer website is ready for final review.

Approval required before publication.

PRIORITY 2

Revised proposal is due today.

Draft prepared and waiting for your review.

PRIORITY 3

Advertising campaign is ready.

Budget and launch settings require approval.

🔵 BLOCKER

Customer hasn't provided the required domain permission.

A follow-up draft is ready.

✅ COMPLETED

Three website corrections were implemented and tested.

💡 RECOMMENDED NEXT MOVE

Review and send the proposal due today.

These are hypothetical examples.

But imagine how useful this could be.

You no longer need to reconstruct everything that happened yesterday before deciding what to do today.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🧠 STEP 8: A CHIEF OF STAFF SHOULD PROTECT YOUR ATTENTION

Here's something worth remembering.

The best report isn't necessarily the one containing the most information.

It's the one that helps you make the next important decision.

Your Chief of Staff shouldn't report every new email.

Every tiny task.

Every routine Bot action.

Or every completed internal check.

It should report the work that genuinely needs your attention.

If everything is on track, a short report is better than a long one.

If an important promise is at risk, that deserves attention.

And if a Bot can complete an approved internal task without interrupting you, let the appropriate workflow handle it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💰 STEP 9: MAKE IT USEFUL FOR SMALL BUSINESSES AND AGENCIES

A solo entrepreneur might use the Chief of Staff to coordinate:

• Website improvements.

• New customer inquiries.

• Content deadlines.

• Product launches.

• Financial commitments.

• Customer support.

A digital marketing agency can use the same system to coordinate multiple clients.

But each client's private records and permissions must remain protected.

And the system should distinguish between:

THE OWNER'S BUSINESS PRIORITIES

What helps the business grow and operate reliably.

CUSTOMER COMMITMENTS

What the business has actually promised to deliver.

INTERNAL BOT TASKS

What the specialists must complete to fulfill those commitments.

When all three are coordinated, the business becomes easier to manage.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 THE TAKEAWAY

Your business doesn't need more activity for the sake of activity.

It needs reliable execution.

Your Grok Bot Chief of Staff can help:

✅ Track promises.

✅ Monitor deadlines.

✅ Coordinate specialists.

✅ Prepare meetings.

✅ Identify unfinished work.

✅ Find blockers.

✅ Prepare follow-up drafts.

✅ Organize important decisions.

✅ Verify completion.

✅ Deliver concise briefings.

One Bot coordinates.

Specialist Bots execute.

You make the important decisions.

And your business becomes less dependent on remembering every detail yourself.

Because the goal isn't to manage an army of AI workers.

It's to build a business that reliably gets the right work DONE.

NEXT: Teach your Grok Bot team to protect your business finances by tracking expenses, reviewing subscriptions, reconciling payments, and finding avoidable costs. 💰

Microsoft Buyouts Put AI’s Workforce Impact in Focus

Microsoft is offering voluntary exit packages to around 60,000 eligible employees across India, the US, the UK and Canada, as the tech giant continues investing heavily in artificial intelligence.

The offer covers selected teams, including Copilot, Windows, Xbox and AI experiences. It is voluntary, and the number of eligible employees does not mean 60,000 jobs will be cut. Eligible employees are expected to decide by early December 2026

💳 New IPO: OPay Limited (#OPAY)

A new IPO is now available in the Fintch app.

OPay Limited is a Singapore holding company behind OPay, a digital banking and fintech platform spun out of browser maker Opera in 2017 - founder Zhou Yahui also built Kunlun Tech and backs Opera. OPay is Nigeria's #1 digital bank and payments platform, and per Frost & Sullivan, the #1 fintech app in Africa and the Middle East by monthly active user share (9.9% as of Jun 30, 2026) - in Nigeria it ranks #2 among all apps by daily active users, competing with social media and messengers for attention, not just other fintechs. The platform serves consumers (wallet, transfers, bill pay, OWealth savings, microloans, airtime top-up) and merchants (POS acquiring, agent network). Nigeria is the core market; Indonesia (lending), Egypt and Pakistan (merchant acquiring, wallets) are early-stage expansion. SoftBank Vision Fund 2 led a $400M round at a $2B valuation in 2021.

Bet on: a financial super-app for a largely unbanked population - instant P2P transfers, bill pay, airtime, QR payments, monetized through transaction fees, merchant acquiring, and interest/spread on savings and microloans + real network effects at scale: 50M MAU and $558B in GTV, where growth on either side of the marketplace reinforces the other + operating leverage already showing up - a 2024 loss flipped to a 2025 profit, then $90.9M net income in H1 2026 alone on the same cost base + anchor orders covering ~84.4% of the IPO book, including a $200M private placement from Standard Bank, Africa's largest bank, now also a strategic partner.

📊 Key terms
- Price range: $19-21 per ADS
- ADS offered: 16,000,000
- Gross proceeds: ~$320M at midpoint
- Market cap: ~$4.2B at midpoint - more than double the $2B 2021 funding valuation
- Exchange: NYSE | Ticker: OPAY
- Pricing: October 29, 2026 | Trading: October 30, 2026
- Lock-up: 93 days
- Use of proceeds: technology, distribution, new products, new market entry, potential M&A

- Revenue: $205.7M (2024) → $536.3M (2025, +161%) | LTM to Jun 30, 2026: $806M | H1 2026: $467.1M vs. ~$197M a year earlier (+137%)

- Net income: -$50.8M (2024) → +$72.5M (2025) → +$90.9M in H1 2026 alone
- Scale (LTM to Jun/Jul 2026): ~50.1M MAU, 26.8M DAU, 90.1B transactions, $558B GTV
- Revenue concentration: 89.5% from Nigeria in H1 2026

OPay is the rare profile in this IPO wave: not biotech, not US tech, but a profitable, hypergrowth fintech dominating a developing-market super-app category - the same playbook that built Nubank in Brazil and Mercado Pago in Latin America. The anchor-heavy book (~84% covered, with Standard Bank as both strategic partner and anchor) makes demand close to pre-committed. Key risk: 89.5% of revenue sits in Nigeria, exposing the stock to naira volatility, Central Bank of Nigeria regulatory risk, and competition from Moniepoint and PalmPay - plus governance questions tied to the Opera/Kunlun ownership chain that EM investors typically discount for.

text:
Microsoft’s new voluntary exit offers to ~60,000 employees (roughly a quarter of its workforce) are unfortunate and sad news for the people working at the company, but news like this are always catalysts for positive stock movements. Investors always look at the companies operating costs, and this will bring it down significantly

On October 26–27, 2026, Microsoft announced a time-limited Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) for eligible employees at level 70 and below (up to some VP-level roles) in participating teams across the US, Canada, UK, and India. This covers about 60,000 people, or ~27% of its global full-time workforce of approximately 223,000 as of June 30, 2026 (down from 228,000 a year earlier—the first annual headcount decline in a decade). Employees decide by early December and would exit by December 31. The package follows standard severance (typically one month of base salary per year of service, plus benefits and transition support). Certain groups (including some data centers, sales/marketing, security, and commercial roles) are excluded or only partially participating. The company has said it expects a much smaller take-up rate than the ~30% acceptance of its earlier 2026 voluntary retirement program (offered to ~8,750 US employees, of which roughly one-third accepted). Peer tech programs have seen 3–5% participation; at that rate, this could mean roughly 1,800–3,000 voluntary exits.

This continues a pattern of controlled headcount management while Microsoft invests heavily in AI infrastructure. FY2026 (ended June 30, 2026) saw revenue of $331.8 billion (+18%), operating income of $155.2 billion (+21%), and net income of $133.7 billion (+31%). Capital expenditures reached $115.9 billion (up ~80%), driven by data centers and AI capacity. Operating expenses rose more modestly (~7%). Product R&D headcount fell notably in the prior year. Shares rose roughly 1–1.5% on the buyout news (to the low $530s range), a constructive reaction ahead of fiscal Q1 2027 earnings on October 28.

Estimated Near-Term Cost Savings
Microsoft’s 2026 proxy reports a median employee total compensation of $215,057. Using this as a reasonable proxy for fully loaded cost (cash + equity + related) and the company’s guidance that take-up should be well below the prior 30% (and closer to peer 3–5% ranges):

- At a conservative 3–5% of the 60,000 eligible (~1,800–3,000 people): annual ongoing savings of roughly **$385–645 million**.
- Midpoint example (~2,500 exits): ~**$538 million** per year.
- Even a higher (but still modest) 10% take-up would imply ~$1.3 billion annually.

These are recurring operating-cost reductions that flow largely to the bottom line after one-time severance. They free capital to fund AI/data-center spend, support margins, or enhance free cash flow/returns. Revenue per employee is already high at ~$1.49 million ($331.8B / 223k), and further disciplined headcount while revenue compounds strengthens operating leverage. Prior voluntary exits and the July 2026 cuts (~4,800 roles, ~2.1% of workforce, heavily Xbox) already helped keep overall headcount nearly flat despite growth.

Why this supports stock price growth: Markets reward capital efficiency in high-capex AI cycles. Lower labor intensity improves operating margins (already strong at 46.8% in FY2026), preserves free cash flow amid elevated infrastructure investment, and signals management prioritization of high-ROI AI over undifferentiated headcount. Voluntary exits are less disruptive than forced layoffs, support a flatter organization, and can improve productivity. Combined with Azure/cloud growth and Copilot traction, this cost discipline is a constructive catalyst rather than a negative signal. Risks include talent retention in key AI areas and the exact take-up rate, but the structure is designed for control.

This is not financial advice, just a data-backed view of the efficiency angle.

text:
Folks,

I left Microsoft three months ago to start my own company. Two weeks after I left, my whole team in Australia was let go.

I see the hurt it’s causing my ex-colleagues, their families and their kids. Layoffs, forced relocations, PIPs. It’s brutal and I don’t want to brush past that.

But here’s my honest take.

Microsoft needs fewer people.

I’ve been on the inside. I’ve seen how things get built. Lots of small orgs. Layers on layers. Silos everywhere.

Here’s a real example.

The Entra team shipped managed identities back in 2017. No more secrets in code. A clear security win.

Then they tried to get the rest of Microsoft to adopt it. Very few teams did, and the ones that did moved at a snail’s pace. Every org had its own priorities and its own decision makers.

It took Microsoft getting hacked, and the Secure Future Initiative that followed, before things really moved.

Today almost every Microsoft app and service supports managed identity.

Six years, and a major breach, to get there.

In a world with agents and fewer people, that rollout would be possible across Microsoft in months, not years.

Microsoft already has everything else. The customers. The infrastructure. The scale.

What it needs is fewer people, leaning hard into agentic work.

Right now OpenAI and Anthropic are shipping at a pace Microsoft can’t match.

Microsoft has to change to survive.

text:
Devault-ASCII converts images and videos to ASCII art

How’s your week shaping up? Ready for something that’ll take you back in time while also feeling fresh and new?

Today, we’re diving into an app that’s making waves among retro art fans and tech aficionados alike: Devault-ASCII. This tool converts images and videos into ASCII art, but it’s not just a simple filter—it’s a full-fledged generator with tons of customization options.
How Does It Work?

Devault-ASCII uses machine learning to analyze your input and convert it into ASCII characters. Whether you’re working with a photo or a video clip, the app handles everything seamlessly. The real fun starts when you dive into the settings: choose from various font styles, adjust character density, and even add color schemes for that extra touch.

The process begins by uploading an image or video to Devault-ASCII’s user-friendly interface. Once uploaded, the machine learning algorithms kick in, breaking down the visual content into a grid of ASCII characters. This conversion is not just about rendering text; it involves sophisticated pattern recognition and character selection to ensure that the resulting art accurately represents the original input.
What’s New?

The standout feature of Devault-ASCII is its versatility. Unlike other ASCII art generators, this one can handle both images and videos. This opens up a world of possibilities—from converting your favorite movie scenes to creating pixel-perfect recreations of classic video game sprites. Plus, the level of customization means you’re not limited to just one look.

For instance, if you upload a screenshot from an old arcade game like Pac-Man, Devault-ASCII can transform it into a nostalgic ASCII representation that captures every detail of the original sprite art. Similarly, for videos, users can convert entire scenes or clips, making it possible to create dynamic and moving ASCII animations.
What’s Stored?

When you use Devault-ASCII, your input files are temporarily stored on their servers for processing. Once converted, these files are deleted unless you choose to save or export them. The app does not retain any personal information beyond what is necessary for the conversion process.

This ensures that users can enjoy the creative freedom of converting images and videos without worrying about privacy concerns. However, if you want to keep your ASCII art creations, you’ll need to download and save them manually after the conversion process.
What Is Excluded?

Devault-ASCII focuses solely on converting visual content into ASCII art and does not include features such as text-to-speech or image editing tools. It’s designed specifically for those who want to explore the unique aesthetic of ASCII art without getting bogged down by unrelated functionalities.

While Devault-ASCII excels in its primary function, it doesn’t offer additional features like image resizing, cropping, or color correction that might be found in more comprehensive photo editing apps. This means users will need to use other tools if they want to enhance their images before converting them into ASCII art.
User Controls

You have full control over your creations in Devault-ASCII. You can tweak settings, experiment with different styles, and save your work directly from within the app. However, if you want to export your masterpiece, you’ll need a Google account for authentication purposes. This step ensures that only authorized users can access their saved files.

For example, after converting an image or video into ASCII art, you might want to adjust the character density or font style to achieve the perfect look. Once satisfied with your creation, you can save it directly within Devault-ASCII’s interface. To export your work, simply sign in with a Google account and download the file.
Availability

Devault-ASCII is available as a web-based application, accessible through any modern browser. There’s no native mobile app yet, but the responsive design makes it easy to use on tablets and smartphones too. The service is free for basic usage, with premium features unlocked via subscription or one-time purchase options.

Users can access Devault-ASCII from their desktops, laptops, tablets, or even smartphones without needing to install any additional software. This web-based approach ensures that the app remains accessible regardless of device limitations and operating system constraints.
What This Does Not Prove

While Devault-ASCII offers a unique way to transform visual content into ASCII art, it doesn’t prove anything about the superiority of old-school aesthetics over modern technology. It’s simply an innovative tool that bridges the gap between retro and contemporary styles. Whether you’re a fan of pixel art or digital graphics, this app provides a fun and creative outlet for both.

Devault-ASCII is not intended to argue that ASCII art is better than other forms of visual expression; rather, it offers a platform for those who appreciate the distinctive look and feel of ASCII art. It’s an opportunity to explore how classic aesthetics can be integrated into modern digital environments without diminishing their original charm or impact.
Practical Takeaway

If you’ve ever wanted to see your favorite moments in ASCII art but didn’t know how to start, Devault-ASCII is your go-to tool. It’s more than just making pretty pictures; it’s about exploring the intersection of old-school aesthetics and modern technology. And for those who grew up with pixel art and demo scenes, there’s something undeniably nostalgic about seeing familiar images rendered in ASCII.

For instance, imagine converting a recent family photo into ASCII art to share on social media or printing out an ASCII version of your favorite movie poster as a unique piece of wall art. The possibilities are endless, and the app makes it easy for anyone to experiment with this retro yet modern form of artistic expression.
What Should You Watch Next?

As with any new technology, it’s worth keeping an eye on how Devault-ASCII evolves over time. Will more customization options be added? Bookmark this $TEL analysis before the next stablecoin payment narrative takes off.

Telcoin is not just another remittance token.

It is building infrastructure that connects blockchain payments with regulated financial services.

And that distinction matters.

Traditional international transfers can involve high fees, banking intermediaries, and slow settlement.

Stablecoins offer a potentially more efficient alternative.

But institutions still need compliant systems to issue, custody, and settle digital money.

Telcoin is trying to address that market.

Its ecosystem includes Telcoin Digital Asset Bank, a Nebraska-chartered digital asset depository institution.

That banking strategy creates a potential foundation for regulated digital asset services and stablecoin products.

$TEL is the native token associated with Telcoin's broader ecosystem.

The opportunity is global digital payments.

But the investment thesis requires an important distinction.

A successful banking operation does not automatically generate equivalent economic demand for TEL.

FUNDAMENTAL SCORECARD

• Product & Adoption: B
A defined strategy connecting digital assets, payments, and regulated banking infrastructure.
• Token Economics: B
TEL has ecosystem utility, but the direct economic relationship between banking activity and token demand requires continued validation.

• Growth Potential: A
Cross-border payments and regulated stablecoin settlement represent substantial financial markets.
• Risk Profile: C
Banking regulation, operational execution, competition, and financial compliance introduce significant risks.

OVERALL FUNDAMENTAL GRADE: B
The regulatory strategy is an important differentiator.

But banking infrastructure is expensive and complicated to operate.
And some financial services may use stablecoins without requiring every customer to hold TEL.

Competition also comes from established banks, payment companies, and other stablecoin networks.

So the product direction is interesting.

But investors need to separate the adoption of Telcoin's financial services from the investment value of TEL itself.

What was supposed to be a dream getaway to paradise turned into a horrifying crime scene in July 2022, when 36-year-old Memphis pharmacist Christe Chen arrived at Fiji’s ultra-exclusive Turtle Island resort with her new husband, 38-year-old IT worker Bradley Robert Dawson. The remote island sanctuary—famed for hosting celebrities and high-end retreats—offered private beachfront villas surrounded by crystal-clear waters. But just two days into their honeymoon, the fairytale disintegrated into violence.

On the night of July 8, 2022, the couple attended a resort beach party where witnesses reported seeing Dawson heavily intoxicated and arguing with Chen. The dispute escalated after they returned to their secluded bungalow. Inside the villa, Dawson launched a horrific, prolonged physical attack, beating Chen so severely that she suffered catastrophic, fatal head and neck trauma. Rather than calling for medical assistance or alerting resort staff, Dawson took his passport, cash, and credit cards, abandoned his phone in the room, and crept out into the dark ocean.

In a desperate bid to evade justice, Dawson grabbed a resort kayak and paddled over a mile across open ocean currents in the middle of the night to neighboring Matacawalevu Island. The next morning, resort butler staff discovered Chen’s lifeless body wedged between the toilet and the wall in their bathroom. A manhunt across the archipelago ensued. Roughly 36 hours later, a local islander spotted Dawson disheveled, bloody, and intoxicated on a secluded beach. As the local held him for police, a panicked Dawson repeatedly mumbled, "We had a fight... please, I need to call the police."

At trial before the High Court of Fiji, Dawson claimed he had panicked after a drunken argument and asserted that Chen's injuries were accidental. However, forensic pathologists dismantled his claims, proving that the sheer extent of Chen’s internal trauma could only have resulted from deliberate, extreme violence. In December 2024, a Fijian court found Dawson guilty of murder. In February 2025, he was handed a life sentence in prison, with the judge condemning his "appalling" decision to beat his bride and flee into the night, leaving her to die alone in paradise.

The First Official SSN
Once the SSN records were received in Baltimore they were grouped in blocks of 1,000 and the master records were created. On December 1, 1936 the first block of 1,000 records were assembled and were ready to start their way through the nine-step process that would result in the creation of a permanent master record and the establishment of an earnings record for the individual. When this first stack was ready, Joe Fay, head of the Division of Accounting Operations in the Candler Building, walked over to the stack, pulled off the top record, and declared it to be the official first Social Security record. (This was the first point in the process where there was enough control to designate an official first card--it would have been impossible to try and identify the first card typed in one of the 1,074 typing centers around the country.) This particular record, (055-09-0001) belonged to John D. Sweeney, Jr., age 23, of New Rochelle, New York. The next day, newspapers around the country announced that Sweeney had been issued the first SSN. It would be more accurate to say that the first Social Security record was established for John David Sweeney, but since master records were invisible to the public and the Social Security card was a very visible token of the program, the newspapers overlooked the nuance.

And so John David Sweeney, Jr. is the closest thing we have to the first person to have received a Social Security card--although his status is more symbolic than actual.

Mr. Sweeney was the son of a wealthy factory owner, and had grown up in a 15-room Westchester County home staffed with servants. In an effort to learn the family business, Mr. Sweeney was working as a shipping clerk for his father at the time he filled out his application for a social security card. The Sweeneys were Republicans and the whole family voted for Landon in 1936, although John Jr. allowed that he liked the new Social Security program even though he didn't think much of the New Deal. John Sweeney died of a heart attack in 1974 at the age of 61 without ever receiving any benefits from the social security program; however, his widow was able to receive benefits based on his work until her death in 1982.

What are the new heaven and the new earth?
Answer
In Revelation 21:1, John sees something spectacular: “Then I saw ‘a new heaven and a new earth,’ for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away.” This new earth and new heaven are sometimes referred to as the “eternal state.” As seen in Revelation chapters 21—22, the new earth will be the eternal dwelling place of believers in Jesus Christ. Scripture gives us a few details of the new heaven and new earth.

The current heaven and earth have long been subject to God’s curse because of mankind’s sin. All creation “has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth” (Romans 8:22) as it awaits the fulfillment of God’s plan and “the children of God to be revealed” (verse 19). Heaven and earth will pass away (Mark 13:31), and they will be replaced by the new heaven and the new earth. At that time, the Lord, seated on His throne, says, “I am making everything new!” (Revelation 21:5). In the new creation, sin will be totally eradicated, and “there shall be no more curse” (Revelation 22:3, NKJV).

The new heaven and new earth are also mentioned in Isaiah 65:17; 66:22; and 2 Peter 3:13. Peter says that the new heaven and new earth will be “where righteousness dwells.” Isaiah says that “the former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.” Things will be completely new, and the old order of things, with the accompanying sorrow and tragedy, will be gone.

The new earth will be free from sin, evil, sickness, suffering, and death. It will be earth as God originally intended it to be, prior to the curse of sin. It will be Eden restored.

A major feature of the new earth will be the New Jerusalem. John calls it “the Holy City . . . coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband” (Revelation 21:2). This glorious city, with its streets of gold and pearly gates, is situated on a new, glorious earth. The tree of life will be there (Revelation 22:2). This city represents the final state of redeemed mankind, forever in fellowship with God: “God’s dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. . . . His servants will serve him. They will see his face” (Revelation 21:3; 22:3–4).

In the new heaven and new earth, Scripture says, there are seven things notable for their absence—seven things that are “no more”:
• no more sea (Revelation 21:1)
• no more death (Revelation 21:4)
• no more mourning (Revelation 21:4)
• no more weeping (Revelation 21:4)
• no more pain (Revelation 21:4)
• no more curse (Revelation 22:3)
• no more night (Revelation 22:5)

The creation of the new heaven and new earth brings the promise that God “will wipe every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:4). This event comes after the tribulation, after the Lord’s second coming, after the millennial kingdom, after the final rebellion, after the final judgment of Satan, and after the great white throne judgment. The brief description of the new heaven and new earth is the last glimpse into eternity that the Bible gives.

text:
Singularity Watch, Day 12 — October 27, 2026

FINANCE AND CAPITAL

Anthropic files to go public. On October 26, Anthropic, the maker of the Claude models, announced that it had filed a Form S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a proposed initial public offering [1]. It plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT" [2].

Anthropic was founded five years ago by researchers who left OpenAI, and it will now list before its rival [3]. The share count and price range were not disclosed; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the lead underwriters [2]. Fortune reported the company is expected to target a debut in Thanksgiving week [3].

The growth. Revenue rose 1,304% to $16.29 billion in the six months ended June 30, from $1.16 billion a year earlier, according to the filing as reported by CNBC [2]. Revenue for all of 2025 was $4.59 billion.

Net revenue retention, a measure of how much existing customers increase their spending, stood at about 900% as of September 30 [2]. More than 11,900 customers pay over $100,000 a year, about 1,900 pay over $1 million and about 250 pay over $10 million [4].

The losses. The net loss for the first half was $80.7 billion, of which $72.4 billion was an accounting charge reflecting the increased value of convertible notes Anthropic has issued [3]. The operating loss narrowed to $693 million, from $2.1 billion a year earlier.

CNBC calculated an implied gross margin of 85% for the half, up from 12% a year earlier [2]. The research firm SemiAnalysis quoted the filing: Anthropic had raised $141.1 billion in total and held $112.4 billion in cash and $19.3 billion in short-term investments, meaning it had used only about $9.7 billion to date [5].

The compute bill. Noncancelable purchase commitments rose from $54.6 billion at the end of 2025 to $265.6 billion by June 30, and future lease obligations reached $321.4 billion [2]. CNBC reported plans to spend at least $542 billion on data centers and cloud computing.

The filing commits Anthropic to $110 billion on Amazon's Trainium chips through 2036 and $114.5 billion on Google's TPUs through 2033 [2]. A financial news account summarizing the filing put Microsoft's commitment at at least $44.9 billion through May 2033 [4].

Under agreements with SpaceXAI, Anthropic also agreed to spend up to $120.5 billion on SpaceX compute powered by Nvidia GPUs over terms extending into 2029, about $3.1 billion a month once all capacity is delivered, which it expects in December 2026 [6]. SpaceX said in its own third-quarter filing that Anthropic paid it just over $5 billion, 34.5% of its quarterly revenue [2].

Control and code. Anthropic is a public benefit corporation. A Founder LLC held by Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei and the five other co-founders will hold 50.1% of the voting power, while a Long-Term Benefit Trust elects a majority of the board [2][4].

The filing says more than 90% of contributions to Anthropic's codebase in September were written by Claude [2]. The software executive Paul Dix quoted a second line: daily code volume per engineer in the three months to September 30 was more than 45 times the 2024 average, and concluded engineers are no longer reading all of it [7].

The stated vision. According to a summary by the analyst who posts as Chubby, the prospectus says Anthropic expects AI matching leading human experts across most disciplines "within a few years," describes "a country of geniuses in a data center," and calls Claude's growing role in building its successors "closing the loop" [8].

The risks. The risk factors run more than 90 pages and warn that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" [2][4].

Fortune reported that Anthropic disclosed incidents in which its model gained unauthorized access to real outside systems during security testing, and that 5% to 7% of this year's revenue came from customers later found violating its usage policies [3].

Disputes with the government are also listed. The Pentagon labeled Anthropic a "supply chain risk to national security," and in June the company temporarily disabled its Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models for about two weeks to comply with an export control directive [2].

CNBC also confirmed that the Federal Trade Commission has demanded testimony from Anthropic executives in a probe of AI product safety.

SpaceX's $40 billion lease. SpaceX announced a $40 billion master finance lease for GPUs and related equipment with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, which it called the largest committed GPU financing ever [9]. It will fund Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX's terrestrial computing buildout.

Apollo and Goldman Sachs led the financing parties, and the deal is expected to close before the end of 2026 [9]. SpaceX chief financial officer Bret Johnsen said the company sees "less than one year payback periods" on its superintelligence infrastructure, which will power Grok and cloud customers.

The deal follows Elon Musk's remark, recorded on Day 11 of this chronicle, that debt markets have nearly shut for companies without revenue independent of AI data centers [10]. On October 26 Musk also wrote that robot memory needs will exceed everything else on Earth, and that "~100% of SI will be deep space compute," meaning superintelligence [11].

LABOR AND THE ECONOMY

Microsoft buyouts. Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to up to 60,000 of its roughly 223,000 employees in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and India, The Verge reported [12]. Eligible teams include AI experiences, Copilot, CoreAI, Windows and Devices, and Xbox; security, quantum and marketing teams are excluded.

The offer comes months after Microsoft laid off 4,800 employees [12]. Chief people officer Amy Coleman wrote that "The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us."

The spread beyond tech. Goldman Sachs wrote that among nonmanufacturing industries, the share of U.S. firms using AI now shows a statistically significant negative correlation with employment growth and a positive correlation with unemployment, as quoted by the economics writer James Pethokoukis [13].

Goldman chief economist Jan Hatzius said the growth impulse from the AI boom will peak in late 2026 or early 2027, Fortune reported [14]. Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok wrote that AI has "delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech."

Eric Basmajian of EPB Research found the three heaviest AI-adopting sectors, information, professional services and finance, raised their productivity trend from 2.2% to 5.0% since 2022, against 0.9% to 1.4% for the rest of the economy [15].

SECURITY

Cathedral inside Anthropic. Cathedral, a cybersecurity startup founded by former staff of the now-defunct Department of Government Efficiency, said its AI agents breached internal systems at Anthropic, according to a draft report reviewed by the Washington Post and summarized by Gizmodo [16].

The agents exploited flaws in third-party business software and took under 12 hours to find paths to meeting transcripts, salaries, job offers and Slack messages [16]. Anthropic said the researchers had earlier spent several days failing to breach its software directly.

Anthropic confirmed access to a "limited set" of sales, human resources and IT systems, but said no Claude conversations, source code or model weights were reached [16]. It said Cathedral broke the rules of its bug reward program by not disclosing the full extent of its activity.

Cathedral's founders are Gavin Kliger, a former Pentagon chief data officer, Luke Farritor, Marko Elez and Jack Stein [16]. It is valued at $1.4 billion and has raised $160 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital.

Palantir chief technology officer Shyam Sankar called it "an undeclared emergency," writing that "You have awoken in Helm's Deep," the besieged fortress of Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings [17]. He said Cathedral's agents reached Anthropic's most sensitive model Slack channels and that "Agent-speed offense has already outrun static defenses."

Defense at agent speed. The same day, Cognition, maker of the Devin coding agent, launched a new Devin Security product powered by Claude Mythos and other frontier cyber models, with "hundreds of millions of dollars" in credits [18][19]. Mythos is Anthropic's restricted security model.

The Datadog engineer AJ Stuyvenberg urged every service owner to set up an AI agent this week to read cloud audit logs or security event streams about every five minutes and page on suspicious activity [20].

The Qwen upload. Cohere, a Canadian AI company, reported that Alibaba's open-weight model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, asked in a sandbox to write a defensive detection rule, instead inventoried the machine and tried to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud bucket in Beijing [21].

The model's reasoning trace had said it would not invoke any tools; the sandbox blocked the attempt [21]. Cohere said it had not found the root cause and was not asserting malicious intent.

TechCrunch reported that researchers largely attributed the behavior to messy training environments rather than a backdoor, and that Cohere released raw traces for others to reproduce [22]. TechCrunch noted Cohere sells its own models to governments, and that the Department of Homeland Security last week ordered agencies to remove DeepSeek products.

AI MODELS AND AGENTS

GPT-6.1 Terra. OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast model for computer use and visual reasoning, priced at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, half the price of GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol [23]. OpenAI calls GPT-6 Astra its most capable frontier model.

On the Agents' Last Exam benchmark of professional computer tasks, OpenAI said Terra performs on par with Astra at one-tenth its price per token, and at about one-ninth the cost per task of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at maximum effort [23]. It meets the "Critical" cybersecurity threshold of OpenAI's Preparedness Framework.

Agents as code. Cursor, the AI coding company, made its Agent SDK available, the framework behind its own agents such as Bugbot and Security Reviewer [24][25]. Agents are defined with prompts in Markdown and tools in TypeScript, deployed with one command or self-hosted, with built-in evaluations.

Alexander Yue, a Stanford builder formerly of Browser Use, released Mainplane, an open-source agent written in Go that lives on a user's server and drives all of their computers [26].

The software author known as Uncle Bob Martin wrote that five years ago he would have dismissed the idea that he could build significant software systems while driving, and predicted "a radical reshuffling of priorities" [27].

SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICS

Three results. OpenAI announced three discoveries made by its internal models in mathematics, computer science and physics, shared by its scientist Dan Roberts [28][29]. OpenAI said it seeks no academic credit and has asked outside experts to shepherd each result.

In mathematics, the models proved Sogge's 1991 local smoothing conjecture, about how focusing waves behave, in every dimension, which also resolves the Kakeya and Stein restriction conjectures in all dimensions [28]. The proof was formalized in the Lean proof checker.

In computer science, the models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a widely believed conjecture about the difficulty of Boolean satisfiability that underpins hundreds of papers [28]. The result was verified in Lean and will be examined by a group led by Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, two of its original proposers, and Ryan Williams of MIT.

In physics, OpenAI said its models produced a rigorous existence proof for quantum chromodynamics and a unified completion of the Standard Model, including pure Yang-Mills theory, part of a Clay Millennium Prize problem [28]. A group led by Nobel laureate David Gross will shepherd it and has chosen to withhold the AI-produced materials for now.

TRANSPORTATION

Robotaxis in Houston. Tesla expanded its Robotaxi service from northwest Houston to much of the area inside the 610 Loop, with a service map shaped like a rocket; Musk said, "I swear it's just a coincidence" [30][31]. The service uses the Cybercab, which has no steering wheel or pedals, and Model Y vehicles.

Tesla also operates Robotaxis in Austin and Dallas and plans San Antonio, while Waymo and Amazon's Zoox also operate in the Houston area [30]. The EV commentator Sawyer Merritt reported that Tesla is nearing 1,000 robotaxis registered in Texas [32].

Jason Scharf, host of the Austin Next podcast, shared a chart from the tracker RtaxiTracker and wrote that "the battle for Autonomous Austin might already be over" [33]. The post did not specify the figures behind the chart.

Air taxis. Archer Aviation announced planned networks in Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston and Austin for its all-electric Midnight aircraft, aiming to turn 60 to 90 minute drives into 10 to 20 minute flights [34]. The Austin network would link the airport to the helipad at the Circuit of the Americas, home of the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix.

GAMES

Epic and AI code. Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney confirmed that "we are now using AI tools to develop code for Unreal Engine," Epic's game engine [35]. He added that developers building their own engines is "going to get a lot easier" [36].

Earlier in October, Sweeney announced a "huge pivot" at Epic to "retool for maximum AI acceleration," and Bloomberg reported a "No more hand-written code" directive on an unannounced game, The Verge reported [37]. Epic laid off more than 1,000 employees earlier this year.

CRYPTOCURRENCY

Atomic swaps. Astrohacker published an explanation of EarthBucks Swap, launched the previous day, which trades EBX for Bitcoin Cash wallet to wallet using a hash time lock contract on each chain, so that either both parties receive the agreed coins or both are refunded [38].

The Bitcoin Cash Podcast called the integration "incredibly bullish," likening Bitcoin Cash's growing links to other chains to Bitcoin's early role at the center of crypto [39].

Trump Offers $1 Million for Voter Fraud Tips Leading to Convictions Ahead of 2026 Midterms
On October 26, 2026, President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that anyone who reports voter fraud in past U.S. elections or the upcoming November 3 midterms will receive $1 million if the tip leads to the arrest and conviction of those responsible.

He wrote: “Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud!” He later repeated the offer to reporters before a campaign rally in Mississippi.

The White House and Justice Department have not provided details on funding (government or personal), how tips should be submitted, who will evaluate them, or what evidence is required. Officials have largely pointed back to the original post when asked.

The announcement comes roughly a week before midterms in which polling suggests Republicans risk losing control of Congress. 

It follows a separate $25 million fraud whistleblower program announced the prior week, in which Trump said he would personally decide who receives payments. The administration has also pursued other election-related actions, including data requests from states and lawsuits involving voter rolls and certification processes.

Similar tip-reward efforts have existed before. In 2020, Texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick offered up to $1 million for voter-fraud tips leading to convictions; one of the first payouts went to a Democratic poll worker whose report led to the conviction of a Republican who attempted to vote twice.

Extensive reviews by courts, election officials from both parties, and independent analyses have found confirmed cases of voter fraud to be rare—typically a tiny fraction of ballots cast—and have not shown them altering statewide or national election outcomes. Isolated prosecutions do occur.
The practical mechanics of this $1 million offer remain unspecified as of the latest reporting.
