text:
Pillar I: The Intended Message (Historical & Textual Context)
1. The Davidic Covenant (2 Samuel 7)
The Human Desire vs. Divine Sovereignty: David sits in a house of cedar and desires to build a permanent temple for the Ark of God. Nathan initially blesses the plan from human intuition, but God intervenes that night. God reminds David that He has never commanded a house of cedar; rather than David building God a house, the LORD declares that He will establish an enduring royal house (a lineage and dynasty) for David.
The Covenant Promises: God promises an enduring name, a secure dwelling for Israel, rest from enemies, and a seed from David's line whose kingdom and throne will be established perpetually. Discipline for sin is promised with the rod of men, but the steadfast lovingkindness (chesed) of the LORD will never depart as it did from Saul.
David’s Prayer of Thanksgiving: David sits before the LORD in humble astonishment, recognizing his own unworthiness and acknowledging the supreme uniqueness of Yahweh, pleading that God do exactly as He has spoken so that His name may be magnified forever.
2. The Expansion and Kingdom Administration (2 Samuel 8)
Subjugation of Enemies: David defeats the Philistines, Moabites, Hadadezer of Zobah, Syrians, and Edomites. These victories are not attributed to military genius; the text repeatedly emphasizes that the LORD preserved and gave victory to David wherever he went.
Kingdom Order: David dedicates the spoils (silver and gold) entirely unto the LORD and establishes righteous administration and justice throughout all the land, supported by an ordered leadership structure.
3. Covenant Faithfulness to the House of Saul (2 Samuel 9)
The Search for Grace: David inquires whether any descendants of Saul remain, specifically to show the kindness (chesed) of God for the sake of his covenant with Jonathan (1 Samuel 20).
Mephibosheth at the King's Table: Mephibosheth, Jonathan’s son who is crippled in both feet, is brought from Lo-debar. David restores all the ancestral land of Saul to him and seats him permanently at the royal table as one of the king's own sons, displaying covenant grace where royal custom typically dictated execution.
Pillar II: Deeper Theological Meanings
The Typological Shift from Shadow to Substance (Messianic Trajectory): The physical house David sought to build was temporary, but the house God promised David finds its ultimate fulfillment in Jesus Christ, the Son of David (Luke 1:32–33; Acts 2:29–36). The biological succession of Solomon points forward to the eternal King whose throne and kingdom have no end.
Grace Precedes Architecture: God refuses to be confined to human masonry. Divine initiative precedes human works: God builds the house, establishes the king, secures the borders, and grants the victory. Man does not do favors for God; God extends unmerited covenant grace to man.
Covenant Lovingkindness (Chesed): David's treatment of Mephibosheth is a vivid demonstration of covenant mercy. Mephibosheth has no military value, no claim of righteousness, and resides in Lo-debar (a place of barrenness). Yet, purely on the merit of a prior covenant between David and Jonathan, he is redeemed, restored, and granted a seat of honor. This directly mirrors the believer's redemption: being brought from spiritual barrenness and inability to feast at the Father's table entirely through the covenant blood of Christ.
Pillar III: Exemplifying the Teachings in the Daily Walk
Submitting Personal Ambition to God’s Sovereign Will: A truth seeker may have noble, well-intentioned ambitions to accomplish great things for God. True maturity, however, mirrors David’s posture in chapter 7: when God says "no" or redirects the path, the believer accepts the sovereign boundary without resentment, responding in worship, humility, and gratitude.
Attributing All Deliverance and Provision to the Lord: Just as the text explicitly records that the LORD gave David victory wherever he went, the seeker must refuse to take personal credit for professional competence, financial stability, or physical victories. Dedicate the spoils of labor to the Lord rather than using them for self-aggrandizement.
Extending Covenant Mercy to the Broken and Overlooked: Embodying God’s character requires extending proactive, unmerited kindness to those who cannot repay, offer utility, or earn favor. The follower of God actively seeks out opportunities to lift up the afflicted and sit with them in fellowship, remembering their own former condition as recipients of divine mercy.
The Synthesized Message
The foundational lesson of 2 Samuel 7–9 is that God’s redemptive purpose rests entirely upon His sovereign covenant and unmerited grace, not on the adequacy of human effort. Man seeks to build an earthly monument for God, but God establishes an eternal dynasty in Christ that outlasts all human kingdoms.
The true walk of faith does not consist of striving to earn divine favor or boasting in personal triumphs, but in humbly bowing before God's promises, attributing every victory to His hand, and extending the same unyielding covenant mercy (chesed) to the broken, crippled, and forgotten that the Father has extended through the Son.

💚 𓂀 In ancient Egypt, green was a color of life, renewal, and the promise that something could return after it seemed lost.

That meaning makes the gemstone imagery here feel especially fitting. Egyptians valued green and blue-green materials such as malachite, turquoise, and faience not simply because they were beautiful, but because color itself carried symbolism. Green could evoke fresh vegetation, fertility, health, and regeneration, while turquoise was associated with protection, joy, and the life-giving brilliance of the sky and Nile landscape.

Jewelry brought those ideas directly onto the body.

Broad collars, bracelets, rings, and amulets could communicate wealth and status, but they could also carry religious meaning. A jewel might honor a deity, offer protection, symbolize rebirth, or help connect the wearer with forces believed to exist beyond the visible world.

I love how ancient Egyptian adornment could turn beauty into a language. Gold suggested permanence and divine radiance. Green promised renewal. Blue recalled the heavens and sacred waters. Even the smallest stone could say something about what the wearer valued or hoped the gods would protect. ☥

Standing beneath temple columns with green stones catching the light, I can imagine how powerful that symbolism must have felt.

Not simply beautiful.

Alive.

Protected.

Renewed. ✨

If you could choose one ancient Egyptian gemstone to wear every day, would you pick turquoise for protection, malachite for renewal, lapis lazuli for the heavens, or carnelian for vitality?

priest at Antioch then Bishop of Constantinople, Doctor of the Church
Homilies on the Acts of the apostles, no. 20
To be leaven in the dough

Is there anything more ridiculous than a christian who couldn't care less about other people? Don't use your poverty as an excuse. The widow who put two small coins in the Temple coffer (Mk 12,42) would rise up against you; Peter, too, who said to the lame man: “Gold or silver have I none” (Acts 3,6) and Paul, who was so poor he often went hungry. Neither protest your social condition, for the apostles were also humble men of low degree. Don't plead your ignorance for they were unlettered. Even if you were a slave or a fugitive you would always be able to do what lies in your power. Onesimus, whose praises Paul sang, was such a one (Phlm; Col 4,9). Would you claim weak health? Timothy had it too. Yes, whoever we are, anyone at all can be of service to his neighbor if he genuinely wants to do what he can.

Do you notice how the trees in the forest are flourishing, handsome, rising upwards? Nevertheless, we prefer fruit trees in our gardens or olive trees covered with fruit. Handsome, sterile trees..., such are they who are only thinking of their own interests...

If leaven doesn't cause the dough to rise then it isn't a proper raising agent. If perfume doesn't give off scent to those who are approaching, can we still call it a perfume? So don't say it's impossible to have a good influence on others because, if you are a real christian, it's impossible that nothing should happen, this is part of the very essence of being a christian... Brethren, be confident of this very thing: that he who hath begun a good work in you will perfect it unto the day of Christ Jesus. Holy Gospel according to Saint Matthew 22,15-21.
The Pharisees going, consulted among themselves how to insnare Jesus in his speech. And they sent to him their disciples with the Herodians, saying: Master, we know that thou art a true speaker and teachest the way of God in truth. Neither carest thou for any man: for thou dost not regard the person of men. Tell us therefore what dost thou think? Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not? But Jesus knowing their wickedness, said: Why do you tempt me, ye hypocrites?
Shew me the coin of the tribute. And they offered him a penny. And Jesus saith to them: Whose image and inscription is this? They say to him: Caesar's. Then he saith to them: Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar's; and to God, the things that are God's.

Tertullian (c.155-220)

theologian
On the Resurrection of the flesh, 5-6 (©The Ante-Nicene Fathers)
“Whose image is this? ”

At the beginning of the world all things were made by the Word of God “and without him nothing came to be” (Jn 1:3). Now man, too, had his existence from the Word of God because of the principle that there should be nothing without that Word. “Let us make man,” God said before he created him, and added, “with our hand” to express his pre-eminence so that he might not be compared to the rest of creation. “And God,” says Scripture, “formed man” (Gn 2:7) (…)

”And God formed man from the clay of the earth.” He now became man who was hitherto clay (…) That poor, paltry material, clay, found its way into the hands of God, happy enough at being merely touched by them. But why this honor? Was it that, without any further labor, the clay had instantly assumed its form at the touch of God? The truth is, a great matter was in progress out of which the creature  under consideration was being fashioned. It is honoured whenever it experiences the hands of God, when it is touched by them, and pulled, and drawn out, and moulded into shape. Imagine God wholly absorbed in it: in his hand, his eye, his labor, his purpose, his wisdom, his providence and, above all, in his love, which was dictating the lineaments of this creature. For whatever was the form and expression given to the clay, Christ was in God's thoughts as one day to become man, because the Word, too, was to be both clay and flesh even as the earth was then.

This is the meaning of the Father's first words to his Son: “Let us make man in our own image, after our likeness” (Gn 1:26). God made man, the creature which he moulded and fashioned, in the image of God, in other words of Christ (…) Thus, that clay that was even then putting on the image of Christ who was to come in the flesh, was not only the work but the pledge and surety given by God.

text:
Non Hindus sporting religious markers and who do not subscribe their reverence to the deity concerned cannot be permitted to step into any part of an Agamic temple premises not just beyond the flag pole, rule Justices G.R. Swaminathan and P. Murugan of #MadrasHighCourt If such entry is permitted without them signing an undertaking, it would defile the sanctity of the temple concerned, they add.
Judges: "We notice in recent times that there are egregious breaches. Mr.Badrudeen Mustafa, an MLA representing the Madurai Central Constituency where the famed Meenakshi temple is located, went inside the temple premises soon after his election. He claimed that he had a right to inspect if proper amenities are being provided. He also went up the temple towers on the occasion of Kumbabishekam. It is ironical that the said MLA proclaimed that Sanatana Dharma ought to eradicated.  
"We take judicial notice of the fact that a Hon'ble Minister who is a Christian by faith, entered Thiruchendur temple without giving the undertaking required from Non-Hindus. We have the illustrious instance of the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Shri Joseph Vijay who worshipped Goddess Meenakshi after signing the undertaking. The Hon'ble Chief Minister who is a Christian by faith was not asked to convert to Hinduism. He was only requested to affirm his reverence for the deity. This is what we call as an inclusive approach. 
"We recall instances from the holy life of Kanchi Maha Periyava. When some foreigners and persons belonging to other faiths would express their desire to embrace Hinduism, he not only discouraged them but called upon them to show greater fidelity to their faith. When Justice Ismail of the Madras High Court used to visit him, Periyava respected the great judge's sentiments by giving him sandal wood paste instead of Viboothi. 

"Chamchagiri is endemic to our political culture. The party The party workers as a mark of sycophancy hang around their leader. They tend to make a bee-line for him. Whether the occasion is appropriate is beside the point. A jocular instance comes to our mind. A well known Minister was having a good time in a spa. Somehow word spread around. Soon, a good number of Chamchas obsequiously entered the spa and offered their pranams. Much to the acute embarrassment of the Neta. One can imagine how the party workers would conduct themselves when they come to know that their leader, be he an MLA or Minister, is to visit their local temple. Out of sheer enthusiasm, they will follow suit without bothering if they can enter the premises or not. We take judicial notice of a video doing rounds in the social media of persons wearing skull caps, pushing their way through in Thiruvannamali Arunachaleswarar temple, notwithstanding the vigorous protests of the devotees. The HR&CE staff stood as mute spectators.

"Not only Chamchagiri but also optics matters in a democracy. We know of one political leader, who is a fundamentalist subscribing to a non-Hindu faith. But he would make it a point to visit the temple and also prominently display the religious mark on his forehead. This was to play to the gallery. The vote value of such a display, is obvious. We hold that usages and customs of temple cannot kneel down before such display of Chamchagiri and optics."    
Thangam Venkatesh versus State of Tamil Nadu (WP MD 30452/26)

This year's December concert series continues the center's role as a venue for community entertainment along the Alabama Gulf Coast. text:
MARKET UPDATE — TUESDAY, 27 OCTOBER 2026

AI got its swagger back overnight. Anthropic finally opened its books, Asia's chip stocks roared and US futures are edging higher.

But read the small print: the AI boom is now being paid for with the biggest loans and share sales in history, borrowing costs are pressing against 5%, and tomorrow the Fed, Microsoft and Alphabet all deliver their verdicts on the same day.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 AI: THE BOOKS ARE OPEN — AND SO IS THE CHEQUEBOOK

💠 Anthropic published its IPO filing on Monday, showing fast-growing first-half revenue and a $112bn cash pile.

💡 An IPO filing is the document a company must publish before selling shares to the public. It is the first time outsiders see the real numbers.

💠 Relief followed. The Nasdaq 100 closed 1% higher, because investors had spent months asking whether AI labs would ever earn enough to justify the spending. It is still down more than 5% over the past month.

💠 Hours later came the biggest AI debt deal ever: $63bn, codenamed "Project North Star".

🔸 A specially created company borrows the money, buys AI chips designed by Broadcom and Google, and leases them to Anthropic. Anthropic's rent repays the loans.

🔸 Broadcom guarantees the main lenders (Bank of America, Citi, Morgan Stanley) against losses if Anthropic cannot pay. Blackstone is funding half of an $18bn riskier slice that carries no guarantee.

🔸 The WSJ reports banks nearly walked away. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan held weekend talks and agreed to pay higher interest rates to get it over the line.

🔸 The loop: Anthropic expects to pay more than $125.2bn to lease Broadcom chips, while Broadcom and Google have committed $42bn and $20bn respectively to Anthropic.

💡 Critics call this "circular financing": suppliers help fund their customers so the customers can keep buying from them. It works brilliantly while demand holds, and magnifies the pain if it doesn't.

💠 The same day, the rest of Big Tech went shopping for cash:

🔸 Meta plans to raise $95bn by selling new shares — $35bn now, $60bn gradually from early 2027 — with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom offering up to $5bn. The stock fell 1.9% on Monday after a 9% drop last week.

🔸 SpaceX struck a $40bn AI chip-financing deal led by Apollo.

🔸 Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to up to 60,000 staff (out of about 223,000) while spending $175bn on AI this year. Its free cash flow fell 23% last quarter to $19.6bn.

💡 Selling new shares means each existing share owns a slightly smaller slice of the company. Firms do it when they need more cash than profits and borrowing can comfortably provide.

💠 The warning light: lenders are getting indigestion. Morgan Stanley has struggled to sell a roughly $300m bond tied to a Lambda data centre, even after roughly doubling the interest on offer. And the North Star banks won't sell about $22bn of bonds until the chips arrive next year — if rates jump before then, they could take losses.

The AI question has changed. It is no longer "is the demand real?" but "who pays, and at what interest rate?" That is why the bond market matters so much this week.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 MARKETS: CAUTIOUS GREEN

💠 US futures: S&P 500 +0.27% (7,735), Dow +0.33% (52,725), Nasdaq 100 +0.42% (29,561), recovering from a flat, slightly softer start.

💠 The VIX fell 3.3% to 17.78.

💡 The VIX is Wall Street's "fear gauge". Lower means calmer.

💠 Asia caught Monday's AI wave: South Korea's Kospi rose as much as 4% (SK Hynix +6.2%, Samsung +4.6%) and Japan's Nikkei about 2% (SoftBank up as much as 6.7%, though still down more than a quarter in a month). China sat it out: CSI 300 -0.2%, Hang Seng -0.5%.

💠 Europe: Euro Stoxx 50 +0.69%.

💠 Beneath the surface, money is still drifting into defensive stocks. Goldman Sachs's risk-appetite gauge fell to -0.5, its lowest since April 2025.

"Historically, readings below -1 and in particular near -2 have been useful contrarian signals." — Goldman Sachs analysts

💡 In plain English: when investors are truly terrified, it has often been a good time to buy. Today they are nervous, not panicking.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 BONDS & THE FED: THE 5% WALL

💠 The US 10-year yield slipped to 4.974%, the 2-year to 4.691% and the 30-year to 5.297% — tiny moves, but the 10-year is still a whisker from 5%.

💡 A yield is the return investors demand to lend to the US government. Higher yields push up mortgage and loan rates and make shares look less attractive by comparison.

💠 The Fed decides tomorrow under Chair Kevin Warsh. Markets see only about a 10% chance of a hike this week, but around 80% for a hike in December (CME FedWatch).

💡 Note the direction: the debate is about RAISING rates, not cutting them, because inflation picked up again in September.

💠 Some officials are urging patience. Stifel's Lindsey Piegza:

"Most also appear to support a slow or more tepid pace of adjustments."

💠 Watch for a "hawkish hold" — no move, but dissenters wanting a hike. Analysts say that would firm up December and lift the dollar further.

💠 Today's test: a $70bn auction of 5-year Treasuries (1:00 p.m. ET), after weak demand for Monday's 2-year sale.

💡 An auction is the government borrowing money. Weak demand forces it to offer higher yields.

💠 The dollar index is at 102.19, close to its six-month high of 102.58. A packed central-bank week — Bank of Canada, ECB (Thursday), Bank of Japan, RBNZ — keeps currencies twitchy.

💠 Japan's case for a rate rise strengthened: a trend-inflation gauge hit a three-year high and corporate services prices rose 3.7% year on year.

💠 France got a reprieve. Moody's held its rating, and the 10-year yield fell from 5.14% to 4.90%. The gap over Germany narrowed from 1.78 points (highest since 2011) to 1.55.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 OIL & THE MIDDLE EAST

💠 Brent crude is around $111, little changed after Monday's fall helped lift stocks. Attacks on Gulf shipping continue; a vessel was seen on fire southeast of Iraq, per the UK military's maritime agency UKMTO.

💡 The chain: oil above $110 feeds into fuel, freight and airfares → keeps inflation high → keeps the Fed leaning towards hikes → pressures stocks.

💠 Israel votes today. Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel must finish the job of toppling Iran's regime; challenger Gadi Eisenkot wants to turn military gains into diplomatic ones. The result could shape the course of the US-Israeli war with Iran.

💠 Diplomacy and escalation are running side by side:

🔸 Officials from Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia (recent defence-pact partners) met Iran's president in Tehran and agreed to keep talking.

🔸 The Saudi-led coalition intercepted Houthi missiles and drones; Egypt's parliament authorised President Sisi to send military support to Saudi Arabia.

💠 US midterms next Tuesday (3 November) add another layer of uncertainty to the risk premium in oil.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 EMERGING MARKETS: BRAZIL'S BRUTAL MONDAY

💠 Lula's surprise re-election sent the 'real' down 8% against the dollar, its worst day since 1999, while the Bovespa index lost 13.9%.

💡 Investors fear more spending with no clear way to pay for it. Brazil already runs a deficit of 9.5% of GDP, debt of 83% of GDP and interest rates of 13.75%, and campaign promises are estimated at R$298bn ($55bn).

💠 Markets now want a credible finance minister and real spending cuts. Right-wing gains in Congress may act as a brake, but Eurasia Group doubts a first package will be enough.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 COMPANIES: THE CONSUMER WOBBLES

💠 HSBC fell more than 6% on slower-than-expected profit growth, despite a share buyback of up to $1bn.

💠 Two warning signs from household spending: Whirlpool slumped over 8% premarket after guiding to a full-year loss of $1.30 a share, and Reckitt cut its outlook on weak North American sales. Today's consumer-confidence reading matters.

💠 Novartis rose after raising its full-year guidance.

💠 Deal watch: DoorDash is in advanced talks to buy Instacart, potentially valuing it around $17bn (WSJ).

💠 Reporting today: Coca-Cola, Boeing, UPS, PayPal and Corning before the open; Visa, Robinhood and SK Hynix after the close.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 CRYPTO: WATCHING FROM THE SIDELINES

💠 Bitcoin is at $79,894 (-0.14%) and Ether at $2,315 (-0.23%), missing out on the AI relief rally.

💡 With US yields near 5% and the dollar firm, assets that pay no income struggle to attract fresh money. Robinhood (tonight) and Coinbase (Thursday) will show how active retail traders still are.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 CALENDAR

Today (ET):

🔸 8:30 a.m. — Durable goods orders (Sept)

🔸 9:00 a.m. — Case-Shiller home prices (Aug)

🔸 10:00 a.m. — New home sales, Conference Board consumer confidence, Richmond Fed index

🔸 11:30 a.m. — Atlanta Fed GDPNow (Q3)

🔸 1:00 p.m. — $70bn 5-year auction result

🔸 Fed's two-day meeting begins

Coming up:

🔸 Wed — Fed decision; Microsoft, Alphabet, ServiceNow, Ford, GE Vernova

🔸 Thu — Q3 GDP, PCE inflation, ECB decision; Amazon, Intel, Eli Lilly, Mastercard, Coinbase

🔸 Fri — Employment cost index; Exxon, Chevron, AbbVie

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 WHAT IT MEANS

🔸 AI is now a bond-market story. Record deals prove the money can be found, but only at higher prices — which ties tech stocks directly to yields.

🔸 The ceiling on stocks is a 10-year yield near 5%, oil above $110 and an 80% chance of a December hike. The 5-year auction and Warsh's tone are today's and tomorrow's tells.

🔸 Wednesday is the big one: Microsoft and Alphabet must show AI spending turning into revenue on the same day the Fed speaks. Weak numbers plus a hawkish Fed is the mix that could turn caution into panic.

🔸 Sentiment is wary, not washed out — useful context if a sell-off comes.

Bull case: Anthropic's numbers, record capital raised, a patient Fed and Middle East diplomacy easing oil let the AI rally resume from a sturdier base.

Bear case: a hawkish Fed sends yields through 5%, debt markets choke on AI supply, and an election result that prolongs the war keeps oil high.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💭 THOUGHT FOR THE DAY

"Never let the future disturb you. You will meet it, if you have to, with the same weapons of reason which today arm you against the present." — Marcus Aurelius

Tomorrow is a huge day. You don't need to predict it — just be prepared for it.

Tech giant Microsoft has offered a voluntary exit scheme to nearly 60,000 employees across India, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Canada. In an official blog post, Chief People Officer Amy Coleman confirmed that eligible employees in these four nations can opt for the voluntary exit program as the company evaluates evolving workforce needs while focusing on essential skills.

The decision comes as rapid expansion and investment in Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology drive up operational spending, with global investments in AI data centers expected to surpass $700 billion this year, significantly increasing costs for memory chips, processors, and electricity. This program follows a previous workforce restructuring in July, during which Microsoft trimmed 4,800 positions, roughly 2.1% of its 223,000 global workforce, primarily affecting its Xbox video gaming division.

text:
$SPGI Q3 2026 earnings: S&P Global raises its 2026 outlook and reviews Capital IQ

S&P Global is leaning harder into credit ratings and market benchmarks while preparing to part with its flagship Capital IQ desktop business. Third-quarter revenue rose 7% to $3.68 billion as a 20% jump in Indices made up for bond-rating growth slowing to 2%. Chief executive Martina Cheung raised the full-year revenue and adjusted profit outlook, though by our math the plan still implies fourth-quarter revenue growth slows to about 3%.

• Sales from businesses owned a year ago: +𝟕% (in constant currency ($3,629M))
• Profit per share, excluding one-offs: $𝟒.𝟓𝟖 (+9% from a year ago)
• Indices revenue: $𝟓𝟓𝟒𝐌 (+20% from a year ago)
• Full-year revenue outlook: 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝟏 𝐩𝐭 (middle of the range: 7.9% growth)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because management raised the full-year outlook, Energy rebounded to 6% growth, and a potential Capital IQ separation would remove the company's lowest-margin business. One caution: putting Capital IQ under review after its division grew subscription sales by 6% concedes that artificial intelligence is pressuring traditional financial desktops and that fixing it requires dedicated outside investment.

The question now is whether shedding Capital IQ leaves S&P Global as a faster, higher-margin benchmark business or strips away the data platform needed to sell artificial intelligence tools to Wall Street. If S&P Global keeps the high-growth data feeds and sheds only the slow desktop, both growth and margins improve; if the whole unit goes, the company becomes even more dependent on debt and stock market cycles. The perimeter details on the conference call and fourth-quarter bond issuance will tell.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐒&𝐏 𝐆𝐥𝐨𝐛𝐚𝐥 𝐏𝐮𝐭𝐬 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐐 𝐔𝐩 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐒𝐞𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧
Just three months after spinning off its automotive unit Mobility Global, the financial data provider is preparing another major breakup. S&P Global said it "has initiated a strategic review of alternatives, including potential separation, for Capital IQ and associated data businesses, which constitute the majority of Kensho Data & Platforms within Market Intelligence." Capital IQ is the company's flagship desktop and financial database for Wall Street analysts.

The company plans to keep Enterprise Solutions and its credit tools, RatingsDirect and RatingsXpress. Removing Capital IQ would shrink Market Intelligence, which has the lowest operating margin of the four divisions at 36% excluding one-offs, and leave S&P Global even more concentrated in high-margin credit ratings and benchmarks. Chief executive Martina Cheung said the review reflects a commitment to "prioritizing our investments where we’re strongest."

What to watch: the exact revenue and profit perimeter of the Capital IQ businesses on the conference call. A separation of the entire Kensho Data & Platforms line would remove more than half of Market Intelligence's revenue and lift the remaining company's profit margin.

🟢🟢 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐮𝐥𝐥-𝐘𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧
Indices, which licenses stock market benchmarks like the S&P 500 to fund managers and exchanges, carried the third quarter. While bond-rating growth slowed down, rising stock markets and trading volumes pushed Indices revenue up 20% from a year ago. Because running an index costs almost the same regardless of how much money tracks it, most of the extra revenue turned straight into profit.

• Indices revenue: $554 million, up 20% from a year ago
• Asset-linked fees (charged on funds tracking S&P indices): $375 million, up 24%
• Sales usage-based royalties (from exchange-traded derivatives): $92 million, up 19%
• Indices operating margin excluding one-offs: 72%, up 2 percentage points

Company-wide expenses excluding one-offs fell by 0.6 percentage points of revenue to 46.5%, helped by a 41% drop in unallocated corporate overhead. That performance allowed S&P Global to raise its full-year revenue growth outlook by 1.5 percentage points, "driven by higher expected revenue from the Ratings and Indices divisions."

What to watch: fourth-quarter exchange-traded fund assets and derivative volumes. Because the raised full-year outlook implies total revenue growth slows to about 3.4% in the fourth quarter by our math, steady market levels would produce another beat.

🟢 𝐄𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐲 𝐑𝐞𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝟔% 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐀𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐐𝟐 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐥𝐥
Energy, which provides Platts commodity price benchmarks and CERA energy research, had been a standing concern after Middle East conflict concessions and sanctions slowed its recast growth to about 3% last quarter. Management kept its 4.5% to 6% full-year underlying growth outlook unchanged in July, which required a second-half rebound.

The division delivered that rebound in the third quarter. Sales from businesses owned a year ago in constant currency rose 6% to $622 million, while transaction sales jumped 37% to $31 million. Energy also booked a $200 million pre-tax gain from selling businesses, likely including its upstream software portfolio, while operating profit excluding one-offs rose 10% to $310 million.

What to watch: fourth-quarter Energy subscription growth, which ran at 5% this quarter. One rebound quarter eases the concern, but Energy needs a similar fourth quarter to finish inside its full-year target.

🟢 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐬 𝐇𝐢𝐭 $𝟐.𝟔 𝐁𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐢𝐧 𝐐𝟑 𝐀𝐥𝐨𝐧𝐞
S&P Global pledged last quarter to spend more than $7 billion on share buybacks in 2026, using cash from the Mobility spin-off and new borrowing. After buying back $1.5 billion in the first half of the year, the company accelerated its purchases to $2.6 billion in the third quarter, bringing the nine-month total to $4.1 billion.

Those purchases lowered the diluted share count by 4.2% from a year ago to 291.6 million shares. Because a higher tax rate held profit growth excluding one-offs to 4%, the lower share count did the heavy lifting, turning 4% profit growth into 9% growth in profit per share.

What to watch: fourth-quarter share repurchases, which must reach roughly $3 billion over the final three months for the company to meet its full-year pledge of more than $7 billion.

🟢 𝐏𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐬 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐭
Three standing growth and cost drivers from prior quarters had no updated figures in the third-quarter earnings release.

• Private-markets revenue: grew 60% in Ratings last quarter, but the release does not break out third-quarter private-market sales.
• Tech-giant bond issuance: hyperscaler debt sales reached $169 billion in the first half against a $250–300 billion full-year assumption; the release does not state the third-quarter figure.
• Enterprise Data Office savings: had reached nearly 60% of its $100 million annual target by mid-year; no new progress figure appeared in the release.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐒𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝟐% 𝐨𝐧 𝐓𝐨𝐮𝐠𝐡 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐧𝐬
Ratings, which charges fees to grade corporate and government bonds, is S&P Global's largest profit generator. After growing revenue 17% in the second quarter against an easy comparison from a year ago, the division hit the harder second-half comparisons that management had warned about.

• Ratings total revenue: $1,271 million, up 2% from a year ago (3% in constant currency)
• Ratings transaction revenue (fees on new bond sales): $677 million, up 1% vs 20% in the first half
• Ratings non-transaction revenue (surveillance and annual fees): $594 million, up 4%
• Ratings operating profit excluding one-offs: $835 million, flat from a year ago, as expenses rose 7% to $436 million

Because expenses in Ratings grew faster than sales, the division's operating margin excluding one-offs slipped by 1 percentage point to 66%. Even though management cited Ratings as a reason for raising the full-year outlook, the third quarter shows how quickly profit stalls when bond issuance levels off.

What to watch: fourth-quarter billed bond issuance against last year's 28% jump. A drop in fourth-quarter issuance would pull Ratings revenue below last year's level.

🔴🔴 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐢𝐞𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐐 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐝𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦 𝐃𝐫𝐚𝐠
"The businesses that are part of the strategic review are strong and have significant opportunities ahead of them as technology changes how customers access, analyze, and use information," chief executive Martina Cheung said. Yet S&P Global also stated that "we believe separate ownership could provide dedicated investment and focus, positioning these businesses to accelerate innovation and growth."

Putting Capital IQ and its associated data businesses up for separation cuts against the claim that they are thriving inside S&P Global. For four quarters, the concern has been that artificial intelligence tools let customers pull raw data directly, bypassing desktop workflow software like Capital IQ. Market Intelligence subscription revenue grew 6% in the third quarter, the same pace as the first half, showing no acceleration before management decided to shop the unit.

What to watch: standalone revenue growth for Kensho Data versus the Capital IQ platform on the call. If Capital IQ growth is in the low single digits, buyers may offer a lower price or leave S&P Global holding the unit.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐀𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Several standing risks and watch items cannot be checked from the earnings release alone because the company reports them on the call or in the quarterly filing.

• Sub-segment revenue splits: the release omits the breakdown between Kensho Data & Platforms and Enterprise Solutions in Market Intelligence, and between Platts and CERA in Energy.
• Market Intelligence contract value (ACV) growth and AI customer counts: management did not print ACV growth or the number of customers using its language-model data feeds in the release.
• Billed bond issuance and debt leverage: total debt stood at $13.06 billion ($2.45 billion short-term) with $2.44 billion in cash, but the release does not give the updated gross leverage ratio or third-quarter billed issuance.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐌𝐨𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐒𝐩𝐢𝐧-𝐎𝐟𝐟 𝐌𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐮𝐞𝐝 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬
S&P Global completed the separation of its automotive data unit, Mobility Global, on July 1, 2026. The company received $1.97 billion in debt proceeds tied to the spin-off, transferred $198 million in cash, and moved Mobility into discontinued operations across all historical tables, booking a $58 million after-tax loss from discontinued operations in the third quarter.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐔𝐧𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟑,𝟕𝟔𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Unearned revenue — cash collected from customers for subscriptions not yet delivered — fell 4.1% from $3,929 million last quarter and sits 6.1% below the $4,010 million year-end balance. While part of the drop is seasonal billing cadence, the contracted backlog continues to trail the 7% growth in reported revenue.

𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐟𝐥𝐨𝐰 (𝟗𝐌 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔): $𝟑,𝟐𝟗𝟗 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Nine-month free cash flow rose 11.8% from a year ago, or 10.1% to $3,510 million excluding one-off separation and legal payments. By our math, subtracting first-half results leaves third-quarter free cash flow of $1,050 million, up 27.4% from a year ago on higher operating profit and lower capital spending.

𝐄𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐚𝐱 𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞, 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟐𝟑.𝟏%  ⇗ accelerating
The tax rate excluding one-offs rose 1.9 percentage points from 21.2% a year ago, following a low 19.8% rate in the second quarter. That jump added $66 million to the adjusted tax bill and trimmed third-quarter profit growth by about 2 percentage points, bringing the nine-month tax rate to 22.0%.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡: 𝟕.𝟒% 𝐭𝐨 𝟖.𝟒%  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from 5.9% to 7.9%
Raised. S&P Global lifted the bottom of the range by 1.5 percentage points and the top by 0.5 points, putting the middle of the range at 7.9% growth. Because revenue grew 9.5% over the first nine months, by our math the updated outlook still points to growth slowing to about 3.4% in the fourth quarter against a tough comparison.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐔𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐥𝐲𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐭-𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐲 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡: 𝟕.𝟓% 𝐭𝐨 𝟖.𝟓%  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from 6.0% to 8.0%
Raised. Management increased the range by 1.5 percentage points at the bottom and 0.5 points at the top, lifting the middle of the range from 7.0% to 8.0% after holding it at 7.0% for three straight quarters. The company credited higher expected sales in Ratings and Indices.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐃𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐏𝐒, 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬: $𝟏𝟕.𝟕𝟎 𝐭𝐨 $𝟏𝟕.𝟗𝟓  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $17.50 to $17.75
Raised. The credit and index group lifted its full-year profit per share target by $0.20 across the range. With $13.86 already earned in the first nine months, by our math the plan leaves $3.97 at the middle of the range for the fourth quarter, down 13% from the third quarter's $4.58.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐃𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐏𝐒 (𝐆𝐀𝐀𝐏): $𝟏𝟔.𝟐𝟓 𝐭𝐨 $𝟏𝟔.𝟓𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠇 cut from $16.35 to $16.60
Cut. The reported profit per share plan came down by $0.10 across the range. The US data provider said adjustments to expected gains on business sales reduced the GAAP number, partially offset by stronger revenue growth.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧, 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬: 𝟕𝟓 𝐭𝐨 𝟏𝟎𝟎 𝐛𝐩𝐬  ⇒ stable
🠅 raised from 35 to 60 bps
Raised. The company lifted its margin expansion target by 0.4 percentage points, and raised the target excluding the sold OSTTRA joint venture from 75–100 basis points to 125–150 basis points. Nine-month operating margin excluding one-offs is already up about 1.3 percentage points from a year ago.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 (𝐆𝐀𝐀𝐏): 𝟑𝟏𝟎 𝐭𝐨 𝟑𝟑𝟓 𝐛𝐩𝐬  ⇘ decelerating
🠇 cut from 335 to 360 bps
Cut. The reported margin expansion target fell by 0.25 percentage points because of changes to expected gains on asset sales.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐮𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐨𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞: $𝟏𝟖𝟓–𝟏𝟗𝟓𝐌 𝐆𝐀𝐀𝐏 / $𝟏𝟔𝟎–𝟏𝟕𝟎𝐌 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬  ⇘ decelerating
🠇 cut from $205–215M GAAP / $185–195M excluding one-offs
Cut. Expected unallocated corporate overhead dropped by $20 million on a reported basis and $25 million excluding one-offs, after third-quarter adjusted corporate costs fell 41% to $31 million.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐃𝐞𝐚𝐥-𝐫𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐢𝐳𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: ~$𝟖𝟎𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇒ stable
🠅 raised from ~$785 million
Raised. Amortization of acquisition intangibles moved up by about $15 million, reflecting recent acquisitions.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞, 𝐧𝐞𝐭: $𝟑𝟖𝟎–𝟑𝟗𝟎𝐌 𝐆𝐀𝐀𝐏 / $𝟒𝟎𝟓–𝟒𝟏𝟓𝐌 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬  ⇗ accelerating
🠅 raised from $365–385M GAAP / $390–410M excluding one-offs
Raised. Net interest cost increased by $10 million at the middle of both ranges as the group carries higher debt to fund share buybacks.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐓𝐚𝐱 𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞: 𝟐𝟐% 𝐭𝐨 𝟐𝟑%  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from 22% to 23%
Unchanged. Both the reported and adjusted tax rate targets remain at 22% to 23%, matching the 22.0% adjusted rate recorded over the first nine months.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐬: $𝟏𝟓𝟓 𝐭𝐨 $𝟏𝟔𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠇 cut from $190 to $210 million
Cut. Planned capital spending fell by $40 million at the middle of the range after the company spent $93 million over the first nine months.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐩𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐬: 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 $𝟕 𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from More than $7 billion
Unchanged. Management kept its pledge to buy back over $7 billion in stock this year, leaving roughly $3 billion to execute in the fourth quarter.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐬 𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐐?
S&P Global said the strategic review covers the majority of Kensho Data & Platforms, which generated $753 million of revenue in the second quarter. Investors need the exact revenue, margin, and organic growth rate of the businesses on the block.

𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐒&𝐏 𝐆𝐥𝐨𝐛𝐚𝐥 𝐤𝐞𝐞𝐩 𝐊𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐡𝐨'𝐬 𝐀𝐈 𝐭𝐨𝐨𝐥𝐬 𝐢𝐟 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐐 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐞𝐬?
Management previously pitched Kensho's artificial intelligence feeds as the growth engine inside Market Intelligence. The release does not clarify whether the AI data feeds stay with S&P Global or leave with the Capital IQ desktop.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝-𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐝 𝐛𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐮𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐞𝐜𝐡 𝐛𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠?
Ratings transaction revenue slowed to 1% growth from 20% in the first half. Without the third-quarter billed issuance table and the update on tech-giant debt sales, outside readers cannot tell if fee rates compressed or volume dropped.

𝐃𝐢𝐝 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐭 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐮𝐞 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐦𝐨𝐯𝐞 𝐨𝐟𝐟 𝟔%?

text:
GALAXY $GLXY Q3'26 — DATA-CENTRE EBITDA SURGES 498%. BUT HOW MUCH OF ITS $455M TOTAL EBITDA IS RECURRING?
Galaxy returned to profitability in Q3, reporting $323M in net income and $455M in adjusted EBITDA.
But the headline earnings recovery doesn't tell the full story.
What interests me most is the growing contribution from its AI data-centre business, alongside the significant investment-related gains driving consolidated profitability.
THE NUMBERS
🔹 Net Income: $323M vs −$85M in Q2
🔹 GAAP Diluted EPS: $0.66
🔹 Adjusted EPS: $0.83
🔹 Adjusted EBITDA: $455M vs −$77M in Q2
🔹 Adjusted Gross Profit: $569M vs $43M in Q2
🔹 Total Assets: $16.4B | +51% QoQ
🔹 Total Equity: $3.0B | +10% QoQ
🔹 Cash, Stablecoins & US Treasuries: $4.9B | +99% QoQ
WHAT'S CHANGING — SEGMENT PERFORMANCE
🔹 Digital Assets Adjusted EBITDA: −$9M vs −$11M in Q2
🔹 Data Centers Adjusted EBITDA: $69M vs $11M in Q2
🔹 Treasury & Corporate Adjusted EBITDA: $395M vs −$78M in Q2
This is the most important distinction in the report.
Approximately 87% of Galaxy's $455M adjusted EBITDA came from Treasury & Corporate, where investment-related gains can introduce considerable volatility.
Meanwhile, Data Centers generated $69M in adjusted EBITDA, demonstrating growing operating contributions from its infrastructure business.
THE AI INFRASTRUCTURE OPPORTUNITY — HELIOS
🔹 Delivered Capacity: 133 MW of critical IT load leased to CoreWeave.
🔹 Data Centers EBITDA: $69M | +498% QoQ
🔹 Helios Phase II: Fully financed and under construction.
🔹 Phase II Deliveries: Expected to begin in Q2 2027.
🔹 Phase II Financing: $3.5B in senior secured notes.
🔹 Helios II: 830 MW of additional approved capacity remains unleased.
🔹 Total Potential Power Pipeline: More than 5.7 GW.
🔹 Data-Centre Capital Expenditure: $757M in Q3 | +69% QoQ
The opportunity is substantial, but the distinction between potential capacity and operating infrastructure matters.
Galaxy's 5.7 GW pipeline isn't equivalent to 5.7 GW of contracted, revenue-generating capacity.
CAPITAL ALLOCATION
🔹 Completed Buyback: $200M, repurchasing approximately 9.8M shares.
🔹 New Buyback Authorisation: $200M.
Galaxy is returning capital to shareholders while simultaneously investing heavily in data-centre expansion.
That makes financing discipline and future cash generation particularly important.
MY TAKE
What interests me most isn't simply the return to profitability.
It's that Galaxy is increasingly becoming a hybrid investment spanning digital assets and AI infrastructure.
The digital-assets business provides exposure to cryptocurrency markets and financial activity.
The data-centre business offers the potential for longer-term infrastructure leasing revenue.
I can see the attraction.
The first 133 MW delivered to CoreWeave is already contributing to earnings, while Phase II provides another potential growth catalyst in 2027.
But I wouldn't extrapolate the $455M adjusted EBITDA as though it all represents recurring operating earnings.
The $395M Treasury & Corporate contribution is materially different from contracted infrastructure income.
And while Data Centers generated $69M in adjusted EBITDA, the company spent $757M on data-centre capital expenditure during the quarter.
Those aren't directly comparable measures, but they highlight how capital-intensive the expansion remains.
The investment case will ultimately depend on converting additional capacity into contracted, operational infrastructure and generating attractive returns after financing and construction costs.
WHAT MATTERS NEXT
I'll be watching Phase II construction, the pace of capacity deliveries, additional leasing agreements, debt requirements and the growth of recurring data-centre cash flow.
My conclusion: Galaxy's AI infrastructure business is beginning to demonstrate meaningful earnings potential. But the real opportunity isn't simply building more megawatts. It's converting financed capacity into durable cash flow and attractive returns on invested capital.
— EMMANUELINVEST

🐀🏠 HEARING SCRATCHING, SCURRYING, OR THUMPING IN YOUR ATTIC? THAT SOUND COULD BE A WARNING! 🐿️🦝
As cooler fall nights settle across Hampton Roads, Virginia, mice, rats, squirrels, and other wildlife begin searching for warm, protected places to shelter and nest. Unfortunately, your home’s attic may offer everything they’re looking for!
From Virginia Beach and Chesapeake to Norfolk, Suffolk, Hampton, Newport News, and Williamsburg, homeowners should pay close attention to unusual noises coming from above their ceilings.
🔊 WHAT ARE THOSE SOUNDS IN YOUR ATTIC?
🐭 Scratching and scurrying at night could indicate mice or rats moving through insulation or wall cavities.
🐿️ Running, scratching, or rolling sounds during daylight hours may suggest squirrels have entered your attic.
🦝 Heavy thumping or movement at night could indicate larger wildlife, including raccoons.
⚠️ WHY YOU SHOULDN’T IGNORE ATTIC NOISES
Rodents and wildlife can create serious problems once they enter your home, including:
✅ Chewed electrical wiring and potential fire hazards
✅ Damaged or contaminated attic insulation
✅ Droppings, urine, and unpleasant odors
✅ Damage to ductwork, soffits, and attic vents
✅ Nesting activity that can worsen when left unaddressed
🔎 HOW ARE THEY GETTING INSIDE?
Mice can squeeze through openings approximately the size of a dime, while rats can enter through holes roughly the size of a quarter. Damaged soffits, roofline gaps, attic vents, and openings around utility penetrations can also provide access.

Portuguese company TEKEVER, based in Lisbon, has supplied unmanned aerial systems to the United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance, Army Recognition reported.

The acquisition follows flight trials, validation testing, and operator training. The systems are designed for rapid deployment and modular payloads to support persistent surveillance from forward positions. TEKEVER said the purchase results from several years of cooperation. In March 2025, its AR3 drone completed an operational exercise with USSOCOM at Camp Roberts, California, including tests under electronic warfare constraints.

The AR3 is a fixed-wing tactical reconnaissance drone with a 3.5-metre (11.5-foot) wingspan, up to 16 hours of endurance, and a line-of-sight range of up to 100 kilometres (62 miles). The upgraded AR3 Evolution offers up to 22 hours of endurance in fixed-wing configuration and a communication range of up to 230 kilometres (143 miles). It can operate from a 5-by-5-metre (16-by-16-foot) area. TEKEVER has not disclosed the exact model or quantity acquired.

text:
Russia has refused ceasefires, Zelenski, however:

Major documented instances where Ukraine/Zelensky did not accept proposed terms
•  Spring 2022 Istanbul talks (and related Belarus/Turkey talks): Negotiators produced draft frameworks (including the Istanbul Communiqué) covering Ukrainian neutrality, security guarantees from multiple countries, limits on Ukraine’s military in some versions, and deferred resolution of Crimea’s status (sometimes over 10–15 years). No final agreement was signed. Talks broke off amid mutual distrust, Russian demands Ukraine viewed as ultimatums (especially demilitarization and army-size caps), the discovery of atrocities (e.g., Bucha), shifting battlefield conditions after Russia withdrew from the Kyiv area, and Ukrainian assessments that better terms were possible. Zelensky has described the Russian positions as ultimatums rather than genuine negotiations and stated Ukraine signed nothing. Claims that Western figures (notably Boris Johnson) pressured Ukraine to abandon a near-deal are disputed; Zelensky has rejected that narrative. 
•  Early 2023 private/unofficial peace plan (reported by the Financial Times in October 2026): An unofficial initiative (involving figures such as Matthias Warnig and presented via Ukrainian economist Oleksandr Rodnyansky) reportedly offered Russian withdrawal from most territory seized after 24 February 2022 (roughly back toward pre-full-invasion lines in parts of Donbas), recognition of Russian control over Crimea, a land corridor to Crimea, Ukrainian neutrality (no NATO), and security guarantees. Zelensky and Andriy Yermak rejected it, reportedly preferring to leverage battlefield gains (e.g., Kharkiv counteroffensive) for better terms. It was not an official government-to-government proposal. 
•  Later US-linked and other proposals (especially 2025 onward): Zelensky has repeatedly rejected elements involving formal recognition of Russian control over Crimea or other occupied areas, additional unilateral territorial cessions beyond the current line of contact, deals negotiated without Ukraine’s direct participation, or arrangements lacking robust security guarantees. He has publicly said Ukraine is ready for an immediate ceasefire/freeze along the existing front lines (with Russia currently controlling roughly 19% of Ukrainian territory) but will not cede more land or recognize annexations, and that any “weak” deal would only prolong the war. He has also stated that in the negotiation process Ukraine says “no” hundreds of times to specific questions and details.

text:
Israeli Mossad agents kidnapped Mordechai Vanunu in Rome in September 1986.
 
Vanunu’s Moroccan Jewish family immigrated to Israel when he was a child. After serving in the Army, he worked at the Negev Nuclear Research Center from 1976 until 1985, suspected by many around the world to house a secret Israeli nuclear weapons program. 
 
While simultaneously pursing a college degree, he became active in student politics, including pro-Palestinian causes. He was warned by his superiors to cease his outside activities but did not.
 
In 1985, Vanunu took photos of the complex, including clear evidence of nuclear weapons development. Undiscovered, he then moved to Australia, where he converted to Christianity.
 
The following year, he offered the photos and story to a reporter from London’s Sunday Times, among others. His information was deemed credible, and he was flown to London for more interviews, where he was sequestered for many days in a hotel, while the story was corroborated and readied for publication.
 
Unbeknownst to anyone, a friend of Vanunu’s had also sold the story to the Sunday Mirror, owned by Robert Maxwell, a former Mossad officer and father of Ghislaine Maxwell.
 
In late September, Vanunu suddenly disappeared from London. He had struck up a relationship with an Israeli-American female Mossad agent posing as a tourist named Cindy. She convinced him to take a short trip to Rome with her, where he was captured, drugged, and smuggled back to Israel via ship.
 
While being transported in a van to court in late 1986, Vanunu wrote a message to camera crews on his hand, which read, “Vanunu M was hijacked in Rome ITL. 30.9.86. 21.000. Came to Rome by fly BA504.”
 
The Sunday Times published the story on Israel’s nuclear arsenal just days after his disappearance, and Vanunu was convicted of treason, serving 18 years before his release in 2004. Afterwards he was prohibited from leaving Israel and had continued legal troubles.
 
The American Mossad agent ‘Cindy’ returned to the US, where she reportedly began a new career as a real estate agent in Orlando, FL.

RT @velitesgear | Full Text Article: https://t.co/LNiR9wzjbx | Author: @militarnyi Indonesian Recruited by Russia Eliminated in His First Battle in Donetsk Region 
Ukraine’s Defense Forces have eliminated an Indonesian citizen in the Donetsk region, who Russia recruited. He died in his first battle as part of an occupation unit after a week and a half of military training.

Defense Intelligence of Ukraine (DIU) reported this.

Taufiq Muhammad was born on May 22, 1978, in Sorong. Before traveling to Russia, he lived in Surabaya on the island of Java, worked as a taxi driver in Jakarta, and as a manager at an agricultural company. He also had work experience in the United States and spoke English.

According to DIU, recruiters found him through a CV he had submitted. The man apparently agreed to travel to Moscow after being promised easy money.

On April 19, 2026, he signed a one-year contract with the Russian army in Korolyov, Moscow region.

 Passport of Taufiq Muhammad, the Indonesian citizen recruited into the Russian army. Photo credits: DIU

The recruit was assigned as a machine gunner and sent to a training center near Voronezh. He spent only a week and a half there before being deployed to temporarily occupied Ukrainian territory.

Muhammad was eliminated in his first engagement, when Russian units attempted to advance from Zelena Dolyna towards Novoselivka and Drobysheve in the Donetsk region.

This is another example of Russia recruiting foreign nationals under the guise of employment and subsequently sending them to the front.

Similar cases have previously been reported among citizens of African countries. In particular, Militarnyi reported the elimination in the Kharkiv region of a 34-year-old Nigerian who joined the Russian military after being offered a job and underwent just one week of training.

 Documents of Taufiq Muhammad, who signed a contract with the Russian army and died in the Donetsk region. Photo credits: DIU

Russian intermediaries may arrange visas and pay for travel tickets for foreign nationals, promising them civilian jobs. Upon arrival in Russia, authorities sometimes confiscate their passports, and instead of the promised employment, they are forced to sign military contracts.

Since the start of the full-scale invasion, nearly 46,000 foreign nationals from 151 countries and unrecognized territories have signed contracts with the Russian army.

According to Ukraine’s Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War, 16,168 foreign nationals were recruited into the Russian military in the first nine months of 2026.

text:
AI Puts India Job Market at Risk

(a) IIT Madras paper shows how AI affects Indian jobs (b) Microsoft India: 6,200 Voluntary Exit Offers (c) India’s IT & Services Based Economy: AI threat dims long-term foreign investor outlook (d) DATA:.

Tech Job Losses Are Real

a. Microsoft India: Yesterday Microsoft announced voluntary exit offers (VEOs) for 60,000 employees (27% of total workforce) in: US, Canada, UK, and India. Microsoft India has 23,000 employees. Avg 27% = 6,200 buyouts in India.

b. Employee Dilemma: If you don’t accept a financial buyout now, you may later be laid off with no benefits. Consider the life of a Microsoft employee who refuses to take the offer now, and lives each day with the risk of a much bigger regret.

c. Oracle India: In June 2026, Oracle cut 21,000 jobs globally, including 12,000 in India. In Sept 2026, Oracle removed another 3,000 employees in India in a second round of layoffs.

d. The Financial Times interviewed an Indian laid-off Oracle employee in Aug. He was lucky to find a job at 25% of his earlier pay. “I have a big WhatsApp group who haven’t got a job. In India, a traditional IT job is totally dead.”

e. In the same Aug report, FT also quoted Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar: “AI will cut a lot of jobs. I can see there could be 50% of job cuts in Bangalore and other parts of the country.”

f. Fitch Report: For global companies, the economic logic of hiring vast offshore engineering teams is becoming weaker. Similar situation also exists in GCCs in India. EIIRTrend projects 25~30,000 GCC roles could be trimmed in 2026.

g. Global banks like HSBC, Barclays, StanChart are weighing deep cuts in back office roles in India. StanChart CEO said: “We do have job role reductions in favour of the machines.”

IIT Madras White Paper

a. Yesterday, Centre for Responsible AI (CeRAI) at IIT Madras published a white paper titled: “How AI Is Reconfiguring Work in India.” The paper identifies the tasks that AI in India is already performing to fully or partially to replace humans.

b. IT Jobs: The paper says: “India’s top IT firms added only 17 net employees in the first 9 months of FY26. AI coding agents have compressed entry-level software roles. System architecture, tech leadership, and resolving complex failures are still handled by humans.

c. BPO Jobs: Voice support in BPO, such as order status queries, appointment confirmations, payment reminders are now handled by voice AI agents. $80B labour costs already cut in 2026; 80% of customer service human jobs going away in next two years.

d. Mfg Jobs: Example: Hyundai’s plant near Chennai has adopted AI visual scanning and digital validation across the assembly process. Quality evaluations using robotic tools, optical 3D scanners, and UHS cameras have replaced manual inspections.

e. MSME Use Cases: Indian MSMEs employ 33 cr people. Several use cases are already commercially deployed by AI vendors. Vendors report substantial gains: reduced downtime (AI does not fall sick), lower defect rates, improved accuracy etc.

f. Bookkeeping, Creative & Research: A human graphic designer costs ₹150-₹3,000 per design asset. AI can do that same job in ₹8-₹10. Similarly, AI legal research tools have reduced need for paralegal work. Routine bookkeeping jobs are handled by AI tools.

Endpiece: For Retail Investors

Institutional investors bet on long-term growth trends; not on taxes.

Indian operators who are daily selling a dream that LTCG tax cut will bring back foreign investors are looking for exit liquidity to offload large positions.

Retail will be big buyers the day tax cuts are announced. But who will be the seller: these same large operators. Retail will become bag holders. That is the original rule of the game.

🔹 Revenue: $3.9B–$4.0B vs $3.8B–$3.9B previously
🔹 Adjusted EBITDA: $780M–$800M vs $720M–$740M previously
The important distinction is that management raised its profitability outlook more aggressively than its revenue forecast.
That suggests expectations for stronger operating performance, not simply higher equipment sales.
WHAT'S CHANGING
🔹 Equipment Orders: $2.18B | +10% YoY
🔹 Equipment Backlog: $7.96B | +142% YoY
🔹 Backlog at Q2: $6.58B
🔹 Nine-Month Equipment Orders: $6.08B
🔹 Power Delivered: 1.2 GW in Q3 vs 1.1 GW LY
🔹 Data Centres: A 620 MW follow-on order brought one customer's cumulative orders to approximately 1.72 GW.
🔹 Additional Demand: A separate 450 MW order supports North American data-centre projects.
🔹 Recurring Services: A long-term maintenance agreement covers the first 500 MW of previously ordered capacity.
THE OPPORTUNITY BEYOND EQUIPMENT SALES
This is where the investment case becomes particularly interesting.
INNIO's Equipment business generated a 17.1% adjusted EBITDA margin in Q3.
Its Services business generated a 31.7% margin.
That's a significant difference.
Equipment orders create revenue visibility today. But once those engines are installed, customers need maintenance, replacement parts and ongoing technical support.
That creates opportunities for recurring services revenue over the equipment's operating life.
The larger the installed base becomes, the greater that potential opportunity.
MY TAKE
What interests me most isn't simply the 57% revenue growth.
It's how INNIO is positioned within the AI infrastructure buildout.
Data-centre developers need reliable electricity, and grid connections can take years to secure.
Distributed power generation offers a way to deploy capacity while broader grid infrastructure catches up.
INNIO is benefiting from that demand, and its growing backlog provides visibility into future equipment deliveries.
But I wouldn't treat an $8B backlog as $8B in guaranteed future profits.
Manufacturing capacity, delivery schedules, customer financing and execution costs will determine how much becomes revenue, earnings and ultimately cash flow.
There's also a financial qualification.
Despite strong Q3 profitability, nine-month GAAP net income declined to $83.3M from $136.9M, partly reflecting $93.6M in IPO and public-market readiness costs.
Nine-month adjusted EBITDA margins also declined from 21.2% to 19.5%.
So while the latest quarter is encouraging, sustained profitability across the full year still matters.
WHAT MATTERS NEXT
I'll be watching how quickly INNIO converts its $8B equipment backlog into deliveries, whether Services continues expanding its contribution to earnings, and how efficiently that growth translates into free cash flow.
My conclusion: INNIO is demonstrating that the AI power infrastructure opportunity is already generating substantial revenue. But the longer-term investment case may depend just as much on the recurring services economics as on the equipment orders themselves.
— EMMANUELINVEST

THE FINAL CHAPTER
YOU DO NOT NEED 100 BOTS.
YOU NEED A CLEAR SYSTEM. ⚙️
A lot of people will read about AI,
save a few posts,
feel inspired for 12 minutes,
then do nothing with it
tomorrow.

That is not what this Playbook was for
you.
This series was built to help you do
something useful.
Something practical.
Something profitable.
Something repeatable.

Something you can actually run
as a business.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

LET’S MAKE THIS SIMPLE. 💡
Over these 36 posts,
we did not just talk about “AI”
in vague, fluffy terms.

We built a real business operating system
step by step.

We covered how to use Grok Bot to help
you:

🔎 research your market

🧠 understand your buyers
📍 improve local visibility and SEO

🌐 clean up your website

✍️ write clearer copy

📣 create ads
📈 track what actually works
💰 reduce wasteful spending

🧪 test ideas before building them
🤝 improve onboarding and support

⚙️ turn winning ideas into repeatable systems
That is a lot more useful than
“use AI to grow your business.”

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE BIG LESSON? 🚨

AI is not the business and your customer (generally) won't care about the tool you're using to solve their problem so long as it gets solved.

You don't have to ever mention AI/SI when discussing their problems and what you propose to do to solve it.

However, if they're so fundamentally anti-AI or anti-tech that you can't talk to them about it without it triggering them into a monologue about data centers or skynet...

...while there's always a way to overcome objections (assuming they actually have access to the money)...
and in service businesses, educating the customer is almost always a necessity...

It still doesn't hurt to do a value check. 

If they're dead set that nothing can convince them that using AI isn't the devil (even if you point out that they use AI every time they do a google search or use the internet)...

...then maybe they're not the best fit as a client for someone who helps them quickly find problems, solve them and automate. 🤷‍♀️

Not every dollar is worth it if: 

-they're skeptical the entire time;
-they can't communicate in anywhere near the same level of understanding/language as you; 
-they're trolling and hate who you are as a person;
-you spend weeks of your life educating because they can't understand why you getting their business info, photos assets or approval in certain areas matters, and -just getting required logins to websites or assets is like pulling teeth:

Remember this:

The business problems and what you solve 
is still the business.

The offer matters.

The customer matters.

The economics matter.

The systems matter.

The follow-through matters.

AI just helps you think faster,
build faster,
check faster,
improve faster,
and document better
work.

If the offer is weak,
AI won’t save it without your input and assistance (not yet, anyway).

You have to train it.

If the website, reputation or what you do is confusing,
AI won’t magically make buyers trust
you.

However, you can train it to make a clearer message.

If your margins are bad,
AI won’t change the math
for you.

But it can expose the math and propose new solutions.

If your delivery is sloppy,
and you don't allow either yourself or AI to commit to a different work schedule and to change the delivery and SOPs
to something better...
then AI can’t create customer loyalty
for you.

But you can let it find the bottlenecks and propose everyone implement the changes...and in a way that it becomes automatic to remember and do.

Good systems beat hype
every time.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

SO WHAT SHOULD YOU DO NEXT? 🎯

Do not try to implement
all 36 posts at once.

Pick the bottleneck in your business
first.

If buyers cannot find you,
start with SEO
and visibility.

If buyers visit but do not convert,
start with the website,
offer,
and messaging.

If leads come in but revenue stays low,
start with your funnel,
follow-up,
and ad performance.

If sales come in but the business still feels messy,
start with operations,
SOPs,
onboarding,
and capacity.

If money is leaking out,
start with expenses,
usage,
and financial controls.

Work the bottleneck.

Then move to the next
bottleneck.

That is how businesses actually improve
in real life.

A 16-year-old student has won a gold medal in Indonesia after developing a fire extinguisher that uses sound waves to put out flames. Ángela Karime Venegas Hernández, from Tamaulipas, Mexico, created the prototype called Vortex Tech, which offers an alternative to conventional firefighting methods.

Instead of relying on water or chemical agents, the device uses low-frequency sound waves to disrupt the conditions that sustain a flame. The invention aims to extinguish small fires without leaving behind the water damage or chemical residue associated with some traditional extinguishers.

The student presented her invention at the International Science and Invention Fair in Indonesia, where the project earned a gold medal. Her achievement brought international recognition to a technical-school project developed through experimentation and repeated testing.
